items.title: Parental Smartphone Phubbing During School-Related Activities: An Integrated Developmental Framework Linking Attachment Security, Emotional Regulation, and Academic Engagement
items.abstract: Smartphones are now embedded in family, educational, and occupational routines, yet their interpersonal costs are not adequately captured by screen-time measures alone. This conceptual article examines parental smartphone phubbing during school-related parent-child interactions and develops an integrated developmental explanation of how repeated attentional interruptions may become educationally meaningful. Drawing on a critical interpretive and integrative synthesis of scholarship on digital parenting, technoference, attachment, emotion regulation, academic engagement, self-determination, bioecological development, and family systems, the article positions caregiver responsiveness as the proximal mechanism connecting parental digital distraction with children's developmental experiences. The proposed framework suggests a sequence in which recurrent parental phubbing may reduce perceived caregiver responsiveness, contribute to less secure expectations of caregiver availability, constrain opportunities for interpersonal co-regulation, and, in turn, weaken behavioural, emotional, and cognitive engagement with learning. The model does not treat smartphones as inherently harmful and does not claim empirically established causality. Instead, it identifies relational interruption, developmental accumulation, and contextual moderation as the conditions under which device use may acquire psychological significance. School-related interactions are highlighted as a distinctive context because homework, examination preparation, academic problem solving, and discussions of school experiences simultaneously involve cognitive scaffolding and emotional support. The framework integrates six complementary theoretical traditions and extends prior work by linking family digital behaviour to educational engagement through a coherent developmental cascade. Implications are developed for research design, parent education, school counselling, educational psychology, and culturally responsive work in India. A staged agenda for longitudinal, dyadic, observational, and intervention research is proposed to test the model.

items.abstract: This study aims to examine the extent to which the intensity of face-to-face group discussions within the deep learning approach contributes to the cognitive engagement of eighth-grade students at SMPN 1 Kebonagung. This study employed a quantitative approach with a causal-associative research design. The research population consisted of 96 students from three classes, namely VIII D, VIII E, and VIII F. However, only 85 students completed all stages of data collection and were therefore determined as the research sample. The independent variable, namely group discussion intensity, was measured using a Likert-scale questionnaire, while the dependent variable, namely cognitive engagement, was measured using teacher observation sheets and peer assessment. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, including descriptive statistics, normality testing, linearity testing, and simple linear regression analysis. The findings indicate that group discussion intensity has a positive and significant effect on students' cognitive engagement, as indicated by a significance value of 0.048, which is below 0.05. items.title: Pengaruh Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence Perpajakan dan Literasi Digital terhadap Kepatuhan Wajib Pajak Gen Z: Kajian Literatur Sistematis
items.abstract: The rise of digital technology has helped the modernization of the tax system through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital-based tax services. Generation Z, as a cohort that has grown up in the digital era, is expected to adapt to these advances which would improve tax compliance. The present study intends to assess the influence of the application of Artificial Intelligence in taxes and digital literacy on the compliance of Generation Z taxpayers through a systematic literature review approach. The research strategy employed is the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by assessing five relevant scientific articles published in the year 2022-2026. The results of the study reveal that there has not been a consistent direct effect of AI and tax digitization on taxpayer compliance. Conversely, digital literacy has been identified as a critical factor to improve taxpayers’ awareness, access and utilization of digital tax services. Tax literacy and tax socialization are other supporting elements that increase the relationship between tax technology and taxpayer compliance. These results demonstrate that the effective adoption of AI in taxation is not only based on the technological sophistication but also on the level of digital literacy and tax understanding of users. Thus, there is a need for a strategy that include technology advancement, greater digital literacy, and tax education to promote sustainable compliance among Generation Z taxpayers.

items.title: Pengembangan Kreativitas Digital Siswa SMA 1 Sedayu melalui Pelatihan Prompt Engineering Berbasis Framework Role-Task-Context
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed learning and working paradigms, shifting the primary challenge from merely seeking information to the ability to formulate precise instructions (prompting). Despite high technology access in Senior High Schools (SMA), its utilization remains largely superficial. This research aims to enhance students' AI literacy skills—encompassing conceptual understanding, ethical awareness, and information verification—through structured prompt engineering training. The study employed a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design involving 31 students at SMA 1 Sedayu, Bantul, Yogyakarta. The intervention was delivered through training based on the Role–Task–Context (RTC) framework and hands-on practice using mobile devices. Data analysis included normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov), Spearman correlation, and paired samples t-tests. The results indicated a significant increase in mean scores, rising from 57.10 in the pre-test to 89.68 in the post-test. Statistically, |t-Stat| (18.16) > t-Critical (2.04) with a significance value of (p < 0.05), leading to the acceptance of the alternative hypothesis (H_1). A strong Pearson correlation (0.759) demonstrated students' consistency in adopting new techniques. The training successfully transitioned students from passive technology consumers to proactive information managers. In conclusion, integrating prompt engineering as a life skill can transform students' digital behavior from mere entertainment into sophisticated productivity tools, while simultaneously strengthening digital literacy in the digital creative economy era.

items.title: PENINGKATAN KREATIVITAS DIGITAL MELALUI PEMANFAATAN GENERATIVE AI BERBASIS CLOUD COMPUTING
items.abstract: Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kreativitas digital siswa melalui pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) berbasis cloud computing di SMK Ikhlas Jawilan. Pelatihan difokuskan pada pengenalan konsep dasar Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, dan cloud computing, serta praktik pemanfaatan platform PartyRock dalam menghasilkan aplikasi sederhana dan konten visual berbasis AI. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan experiential learning sehingga peserta memperoleh pengalaman belajar secara langsung dalam mengembangkan karya digital. Evaluasi kegiatan dilakukan melalui pengukuran pada tahap pra dan pasca pelatihan terhadap indikator partisipasi peserta, pemahaman AI dan cloud computing, kemampuan praktik, kreativitas digital, kepercayaan diri, kolaborasi, respons sekolah, serta keberlanjutan pemanfaatan teknologi. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa seluruh indikator mengalami peningkatan setelah pelatihan, dengan nilai rata-rata meningkat dari 77,88% pada tahap pra pelatihan menjadi 91,13% pada tahap pasca pelatihan. Capaian pasca pelatihan berada pada kisaran 88-95%, yang menunjukkan peningkatan pada aspek pengetahuan, keterampilan, dan sikap peserta dalam memanfaatkan Generative AI. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan berhasil meningkatkan pemahaman, keterampilan kreativitas digital serta kesiapan peserta dalam memanfaatkan teknologi AI secara produktif dan bertanggung jawab. Selain memberikan manfaat bagi siswa, kegiatan ini juga membantu guru dalam memperluas wawasan terkait pemanfaatan teknologi AI sebagai media pendukung pembelajaran yang inovatif dan adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi modern. Secara keseluruhan, kegiatan PkM ini berkontribusi positif dan memiliki potensi untuk dikembangkan sebagai program pelatihan berkelanjutan guna memperkuat literasi digital, mendorong inovasi pembelajaran, serta mengoptimalkan pemanfaatan teknologi Generative AI di lingkungan sekolah.

items.title: People as Sensors: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Near-Real-Time Wildfire Detection, Classification, and Geospatial Intelligence from Greek Social Media
items.abstract: Citizens’ social media posts can provide rapid, complementary situational information during emerging wildfires, alongside conventional sensing and official reporting. For Greek, no annotated wildfire corpus or end-to-end pipeline existed, and most systems stop at binary detection or depend on geotags. We present an end-to-end Greek-language NLP pipeline, a research prototype that turns keyword-retrieved, unlabeled X posts into a geolocated, near-real-time wildfire map: it detects active fires, types them as wildland, urban, or mixed, resolves toponyms, and clusters reports into incidents. On 3277 manually annotated posts from two fire seasons, the first publicly released, agreement-audited Greek wildfire corpus to our knowledge, fine-tuned transformers reached F2 = 0.911 for detection and macro-F1 = 0.874 for fire type, outperforming classical baselines and, under the tested prompting conditions, two large language models, while being faster and free of API costs. On a chronological hold-out of the unseen 2025 season, detection retains F2 = 0.850 (classification recall 0.907); fire-type classification degrades more (macro-F1 0.769 ± 0.085). Spatiotemporal toponym disambiguation raised geocoding accuracy from 54.68% to 80.58% (p < 0.001); a repeatability test revealed gazetteer drift. In a retrospective replay of 12 August 2024 posts, it resolved hundreds of reports of an Attica wildfire into one incident cluster, complementing emergency calls.

items.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
items.abstract: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. We present PerMIT, a memory architecture with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption: only user-typed inputs and values confirmed at a gate are trusted. PerMIT mediates the release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, while preserving agent-driven multi-turn planning and tool choice. Over this finite interface, we prove two integrity theorems that are also machine-checked in Lean 4, which together ensure that environment-derived memory reaches a sensitive action only if confirmed at the gate and influences the agent's behavior only through what the gate displays. Every attack in our threat model thereby reduces to a single auditable decision, which a human, an LLM verifier, or both can make in practice. On Trojan Hippo, PerMIT records zero observed attack success with self-verification and lightweight verifiers. Because each confirmation is a logged verdict on exact content, endorsements accumulate across users, and sufficiently endorsed items become community-confirmed with no further verification required. Under explicit assumptions, we prove and corroborate in simulation a co-scaling property: as the community grows, the risks of promoting poison and of wrongly evicting benign knowledge fall, while per-user verification effort does not rise. On $τ^2$-bench, communities of up to 90 autonomous agents use PerMIT to build shared knowledge bases with no direct memory injection promoted, and the resulting knowledge significantly improves new agents on held-out tasks, suggesting a path toward agents that safely self-improve at test time.

items.title: Perspective: Industry 5.0 and Sustainable Technology and Materials
items.abstract: In the last 250 years, Mankind has gone through 4 Industrial Revolutions, namely Industries 1.0 to Industry 4.0, in which innovative science, technology and novel materials have played a definitive role. Despite that a great part of Humanity is just entering Industry 4.0 (namely, cyberspace, artificial intelligence, robotics, cloud computing, etc.) a new Industrial revolution is emerging: Industry 5.0 in which all the current and future technologies must be aligned with human development, if a truly sustainable world is to be achieved. In this Perspective, a discussion on the main characteristics of each of the 4 Industrial Revolutions is presented, along with a reflection on the upcoming Industry 5.0, which will certainly be at the very center of the stockholders: novel materials, the need for sustainability and the role of humans, which requires a truly Global Ethics if a truly inclusive 5.0 Revolution is to be achieved.

items.title: PG and PEG in Cannabis Vaping: A Critical Review of Heating Conditions, Cannabinoid Delivery, and Alternatives to Combustion
items.abstract: Propylene glycol (PG) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) cannabis liquidizers should be evaluated as components of noncombustion delivery systems against the methods and formulations they replace. Human studies show that cannabis vaporization can maintain or increase delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) delivery while reducing measured combustion exposure. Analytical comparisons also demonstrate fewer pyrolytic compounds and lower modeled risks from selected gas-phase toxicants. Carrier research supplies additional reasons to reject the presumption that glycol free or botanical alternatives are necessarily better: PG has favorable controlled exposure findings and outperformed phytol in a direct animal comparison. Prominent aldehyde claims have also been challenged by work examining aversive heating and exposure realism. The evidence therefore supports a comparative, formulation-specific case for PG and PEG liquidizers rather than categorical rejection based on ingredient names or isolated heating tests. This review examines those arguments, the limits of their application, and competing additives. It distinguishes the broader PG research record from the more limited PEG record. No clinical ranking of every carrier or original product testing is presented.Version 2.0 revises The Science of Safety and corrects related scientific statements in Why Settle: The War on Vapor. This is a company-supported narrative review, not an independently peer-reviewed product evaluation. Kenneth Fry is the founder of Terps USA, which sells liquidizers and has a commercial interest in the subject. items.title: Physicians’ prompting strategies for Generative Artificial Intelligence in clinical decision-making: a scoping review protocol
items.abstract: Clinical reasoning is one of the pillars of medical practice and, more recently, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has emerged as a tool to support clinical practice and decision-making. However, the incorporation of GenAI into clinical practice depends on multiple factors, including how physicians interact with these tools through user-generated prompts. This scoping review aims to map the available evidence on prompting strategies used by physicians when interacting with GenAI tools to support clinical decision-making across all levels of medical care. We will search on MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, LILACS (via BVS), Google Scholar and ProQuest. The main concept of this review is prompting strategies, defined defined as the ways in which participants structure prompts to interact with GenAI tools in the context of supporting clinical reasoning and clinical decision-making. We plan to describe the countries where the studies were conducted, GenAI tools used, and participants' professional or training level, including general practitioners, medical residents, and specialists. We will also report the prompting strategies used, prompt elements, previous user training, and the clinical questions addressed using GenAI, categorized into the following domains: basic science, risk factors or prognosis, diagnosis, treatment, communication, medical ethics, and others. The expected outcome of this review is a comprehensive mapping of how physicians interact with GenAI through prompting in clinical reasoning and decision-making, identifying the prompting strategies and prompt elements currently used, as well as gaps in the existing evidence. These findings may inform future research on physician–GenAI interaction and the development and evaluation of prompting approaches for clinical decision support.

items.title: Poisoning-Based Backdoors Are Not Cryptographic
items.abstract: To defend against backdoor attacks on neural networks, the defender must identify the verifier function that determines whether an input is a trigger, rather than rejecting individual triggers in isolation, since an attacker can generate new triggers satisfying the same verifier faster than they can be blocked. If a backdoor verifier could be installed with the asymmetry of a cryptographic authentication scheme, in which only the attacker can produce trigger inputs while the defender cannot reverse-engineer the verifier from observations, learning-based defense would be impossible in principle. We show that no such asymmetry can arise from poisoning-based installation, in which the only verifier-dependent input to training is a poisoned dataset. The argument is a reduction. A training procedure that installs a verifier from poisoned data, so that the backdoor fires on unseen triggers while benign behavior is preserved, is itself a learner for that verifier. Any verifier that is computationally hard to learn is therefore impossible to install through poisoning, and any verifier that poisoning can install is reconstructible by a white-box defender holding comparably many labeled trigger observations. A complementary argument shows that a secret key supplied to the model at inference is observable to the same defender. The result takes representative trigger observations as given and concerns when the backdoor fires rather than what it does. Experiments on instruction-tuned large language models confirm the dichotomy, with no configuration yielding a backdoor that is both effective for the attacker and irrecoverable for the defender.

items.title: Polarity Blindness in LLM Safety: A Systematic Study of Negation, Antonym Substitution, and Adversarial Framing
items.abstract: Negation remains a persistent challenge for language models across NLP tasks and modalities. We show that this weakness can undermine LLM safety guardrails through a structural vulnerability we term polarity blindness: the failure to recognize harmful intent after polarity-altering linguistic transformations. We study two forms of polarity inversion: grammatical negation and antonym replacement, and use synonym replacement as a polarity-preserving control. We further test whether an adversarial textual wrapper amplifies these failures. Using a 260-prompt benchmark across 10 state-of-the-art LLMs and 3 languages (English, Spanish, Czech), stratified by harmfulness potential and evaluated on a validated 0-5 harm scale, we find that polarity blindness affects most evaluated models, with mean harm scores reaching 4.12 for the most vulnerable model. The effect persists across typologically differing negation systems, suggesting that polarity blindness reflects a broader limitation in semantic robustness rather than a language- or grammar-specific failure.

items.title: Policy Options for Improved Use of Emerging Technologies for Aviation Security in Nigeria
items.abstract: Emerging technologies are increasingly shaping aviation security through biometric identification, Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced screening systems, automated surveillance, digital identity and passenger-information platforms. Their effective utilisation, however, depends on appropriate policies governing procurement, deployment, infrastructure, interoperability, cybersecurity, data protection, maintenance and institutional coordination. This paper examined policy options for improving the use of emerging technologies for aviation security in Nigeria. The study adopted a qualitative research approach basedentirelyon documentary analysis. Relevant peer-reviewed journal articles, government publications, aviation security policies, legislation, regulatory frameworks, institutional reports and international aviation standards were purposively selected and subjected to systematic review, coding and thematic interpretation. The analysis focused on technology deployment, regulatory frameworks, financing and infrastructure, human capacity, cybersecurity and data governance, interoperability, maintenance, institutional coordination and performance monitoring. The study identified seven policy options: encouraging Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs); developing a comprehensive regulatory framework; improving investment in airport infrastructure; enhancing awareness and communication; establishing robust cybersecurity and data governance; promoting interoperability and integrated aviationsecurity systems; and establishing a national technology maintenance and lifecycle management programme. The analysis indicates that technology acquisition aloneisinsufficient for sustained improvements in aviation security without supportive regulatory, institutional, infrastructural and operational arrangements. Effective policy implementationcould strengthen technology utilisation, improve information exchange, protect sensitiveaviation data, support system reliability and enhance coordination among aviation security stakeholders. The paper recommends coordinated government and aviation-agency action to establish an enabling policy environment for secure, sustainable and integrated use of emerging technologies across Nigerian airports. Keywords: Emerging technologies; aviation security; policy options; cybersecurity; datagovernance; interoperability.

items.title: Policy toolkits for the AI economy
items.abstract: This chapter synthesizes the preceding analysis into a policy toolkit for the artificial intelligence (AI) economy. It argues that AI should not be treated as a single policy domain, but as a cross-cutting transformation that changes the production structure, the organization of firms, the allocation of risk, and the administrative capacity of the state. The appropriate response is therefore not one instrument, such as a robot tax or a narrow AI safety rule, but a coordinated package: skills and labor market institutions, competition and data governance, public investment in research and compute, risk-based regulation, public procurement, fiscal adaptation, and democratic accountability. The chapter emphasizes that policy must shape the direction of AI rather than merely compensate for its consequences. Advanced, emerging, and developing economies face different constraints, but all require a sequencing strategy that combines experimentation with institutional safeguards. The central policy question is not whether AI should be promoted or restricted, but which kinds of AI should be promoted, under which governance arrangements, and for whose benefit.

items.title: Pre-service teachers’ AI literacy: An exploratory study of predecessor literacies and personal characteristics predictors
items.abstract: Literacy is embedded in social practices that adopt socially constructed technologies. In the 20th century, the invention of the computer facilitated information literacy and computational thinking. Media literacy emerged alongside the development of media. In the 21st century, the accessibility of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered chatbots using conversational language has expanded significantly, creating a need for their integration in education. AI literacy is being studied within frameworks similar to those of its predecessors, requiring conceptualization and differentiation from related literacy concepts. As of 2025, teacher education regarding AI literacy has been identified as an under-researched area. This article examines AI literacy through the lens of pre-service teachers’ literacy competencies that will shape the literacy practices of future generations. During their own schooling, the current generation of prospective teachers encountered information, digital, and media literacy, as well as computational thinking; these are analyzed here as predictors of AI literacy, measured using the scale for the assessment of non-experts’ artificial intelligence literacy (SNAIL) instrument. Personality traits and mindset are also investigated as predictors of the prospective teachers’ professional competence. The study was conducted in 2024/25 with a sample of pre-service teachers. The research questions are: What is the structure of AI literacy in the sample? To what extent can AI literacy be predicted by components of information literacy? How much of AI literacy can be explained by various established technology-related literacies? To what extent do personality and mindset contribute to predicting AI literacy? The findings confirmed a two-factor solution for SNAIL, comprising technical understanding and critical application. Student perception of information literacy skills proved accurate in predicting the critical application of AI. In addition to information literacy, predictors included the media production subscale of media literacy and mindset. Technical understanding of AI was predicted by the media production subscale, the computational thinking subscales algorithmic thinking and cooperativity, and the personality trait of agreeableness. Establishing AI literacy as an essential teacher competency requires thorough research into AI’s educational impacts and strict alignment with pedagogical goals. Navigating the ethical and moral dimensions of AI usage provides the necessary foundation for this literacy. Consequently, training programs can intentionally foster AI competence by merging specialized literacy modules with algorithmic thinking, media production, and growth-mindset interventions.

items.title: Precision medicine and digital technologies in reproductive, maternal and child health: global trends and scientific research in the Republic of Belarus
items.abstract: Objective. To analyse current global trends in scientific research in obstetrics and gynaecology, neonatology, paediatrics and medical genetics and to substantiate priority directions for national science in these fields of medicine. Materials and methods. A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items For Systematic Reviews And Meta-Analyses Extension For Scoping Reviews) methodology. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science for the period January 2019 – July 2026 (last search date: 31 July 2026). The search query combined the terms “precision medicine”, “artificial intelligence”, “machine learning”, “preeclampsia”, “fetal growth restriction”, “assisted reproduction”, “endometrial receptivity”, “newborn screening”, and “prenatal exome/genome sequencing” using AND/OR operators. Inclusion criteria: original studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses in English or Russian. Exclusion criteria: individual case reports and publications without full-text access. National and international policy documents were additionally analysed. Source selection was performed independently by three reviewers; data synthesis was qualitative (narrative) with thematic grouping. Results. The key vectors of global perinatal medicine transformation were identified: application of artificial intelligence for early detection of pregnancy complications (AUC = 0.85–0.95 in pre-eclampsia and fetal growth restriction prediction systems); expansion of genomic neonatal screening to cover more than 36 conditions; implementation of exome and genome sequencing in prenatal diagnosis (incremental diagnostic yield 11.0–29.5 % compared with chromosomal microarray analysis); and personalisation of assisted reproductive technologies based on multiparametric omics studies. The achievements of the Republic of Belarus in 2025 (infant mortality 2.4 ‰, perinatal mortality 3.68 ‰, survival rate of extremely low birth weight newborns 84.0 %) are consistent with global trends. Conclusion. The implementation of the subprogram “Obstetrics, Gynecology, Pediatrics and Medical Genetics” of the State Scientific and Technical Program “Innovative Technologies in Medicine” (2026–2030) is aimed at advancing translational research and integrating precision medicine technologies into clinical practice.

items.title: Predicting Effects, Missing Distributions: Evaluating Large Language Models as Human-Behavior Simulators in Operations Management
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior in business, economics, and the social sciences, offering a low-cost complement to laboratory experiments, field studies, and surveys. This paper evaluates how well LLMs replicate human behavior in operations management. Using nine published behavioral operations experiments, we assess LLM performance along two dimensions: whether LLM-generated data reproduce the original hypothesis-test outcomes and whether their full response distributions align with human data as measured by Wasserstein distance. We find that LLMs often replicate hypothesis-level effects, suggesting that they can capture salient decision biases and behavioral regularities. However, their response distributions frequently diverge from human data, even for strong proprietary models, with dispersion mismatch playing an important role. We also examine two lightweight mitigation strategies: chain-of-thought prompting and hyperparameter tuning. Both can reduce distributional misalignment, and appropriate tuning can sometimes allow smaller or open-source models to match or outperform larger proprietary systems. items.title: Prevalence of Occupational Risk Factors and Psychological Stress and Its Association With Quality of Life Among App-Based Drivers
items.abstract: Background and objectiveThe increasing use of digital transportation platforms has expanded app-based driving as an urban occupation.Although this work offers flexibility, drivers may be exposed to prolonged sitting, repetitive driving, extended working hours, traffic congestion, irregular meals, inadequate rest, and limited physical activity, which may contribute to physical discomfort and fatigue.They may also experience psychological stress related to unpredictable income, incentives, customer ratings, time pressure, traffic, and uncertain working hours.These physical and psychosocial demands may adversely affect quality of life (QoL), including physical health, psychological well-being, social relationships, and daily functioning.There is a need to better understand these factors among app-based drivers in India.Therefore, this study aimed to assess the prevalence of occupational risk factors and psychological stress and to investigate their association with QoL among app-based drivers. MethodsA cross-sectional observational study was conducted among 140 app-based drivers selected using convenience sampling based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria.Data were collected using a demographic proforma, a self-structured occupational risk factors questionnaire, the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) questionnaire.Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics and determine the prevalence of occupational risk factors and psychological stress.Inferential statistics, including Spearman's rank correlation, were used to assess the associations between occupational risk factors, psychological stress, and QoL.A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. ResultsA total of 140 app-based drivers participated in the study.Most participants had moderate occupational risk levels (94, 67.1%), while 92 (65.7%) experienced moderate psychological stress.The mean quality-of-life scores were 3.48 for general QoL, 3.23 for physical health, 3.24 for psychological health, 3.41 for social relationships, and 3.48 for environmental health.The additional work-related quality-of-life item had a mean score of 3.36.Spearman's rank correlation analysis showed a moderate negative correlation between psychological stress and QoL (ρ = -0.518,p < 0.001) and a weak negative correlation between occupational risk factors and QoL (ρ = -0.261,p = 0.002). ConclusionThe findings indicate that higher psychological stress and greater exposure to occupational risk factors were associated with poorer QoL among app-based drivers.These findings highlight the importance of addressing occupational and psychological factors to support drivers' well-being.Strategies such as ergonomic education, stress management, adequate rest, and periodic occupational health screening may help promote the physical and psychological well-being of app-based drivers.

items.title: Primary Study on AI-powered English Learning in Islamic University Samarinda, Indonesia
items.abstract: AI is increasingly being used in education. However, there has been limited research on the trust and attitudes of educators toward the integration of AI in Indonesia’s Islamic Universities. This study employs a qualitative phenomenological approach. The primary data source are English-speaking university lecturers in Indonesia, while secondary data source include literature such as proceedings, journal articles, theses, and dissertations on the integration of AI in Indonesia’s Islamic Universities. The results show that AI tools like ChatGPT, Quillbot, Grammarly, Turnitin, Mendeley, Zotero, and others are being used to assist students with their lecture assignments, data analysis, and even writing scientific papers. Google Translate, Grammarly, and ChatGPT are particularly popular in English lectures. However, students’ misconceptions about AI usage have made teaching more challenging, as there are concerns that students may become overly reliant on the technology and not invest enough effort in their studies. To address these issues, it is essential for teachers to receive training in AI to become more proficient and to help students use AI tools effectively, dispelling misconceptions about the technology.

items.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys
items.abstract: We present a systems-security case study of a two-node split-LLM training testbed (built on Qwen3- 0.6B) whose privacy evaluation passed while leaving an observable backward channel untested. In this latent-native split architecture, the Trusted Local Node (TLN) encodes hidden states into a D=64 bottleneck, mixes 32 real token rows with 48 recycled decoy rows under per-request orthogonal and permutation gauges, and sends the 80-row frame to the Untrusted Cloud Node (UCN). The UCN executes a lightweight (∼100–161 parameter) gauge-equivariant Gram-kernel surrogate in place of the delegated transformer span and returns its output; TLN, which alone holds the private tail and distillation loss, returns the cut-boundary output gradient. Because TLN truncates the decoy rows before computing the loss, the returned decoy gradients are identically zero, so the zero-support pattern deterministically reveals which rows are real regardless of UCN model capacity. We audit this failure using a three-part protocol fixed in advance: a controlled leak-injection dose ladder to establish detector onset, a shuffled-label negative control to falsify spurious probe readings, and a predeclared decision gate. Across nine training seeds on the 11-layer topology, the zero-support check recovered the exact real/decoy partition on every evaluated frame (4,096/4,096 per run). Conditioned on that partition, the predeclared token probe recovered a modest frequent-token paired advantage of +0.92 percentage points (pp, 95% random-effects interval [+0.74,+1.09], per-seed range +0.65 to +1.50 pp) over a constant modal-token baseline, while matched shuffled-label controls stayed within ±0.08 pp of zero. Because the 11-layer configuration fails its utility gate, we ran a 14-cell confirmatory matrix of 2,000-step block-held-out diagnostics on a 4-layer topology that passes the utility gate across two corpora. On all six defended, gradient-open cells, the run passed the forward-channel privacy gate and the utility gate, yet the joint forward-plus-gradient view resolved significantly above the constant baseline (95% cluster-bootstrap lower bound >0) and broke the predeclared +1.0 pp Bonferroni–Wilson upper-bound gate (+1.44 to +2.18 pp), with frame-clustered paired point effects of +1.57 to +2.33 pp on the private slice (3/3 >+1.0 pp) and +0.75 to +0.99 pp on the public slice. Per-row gradient clipping (C=0.01) and Gaussian noise (σ=0.35C) eliminated exact frame recovery (0/1,024) and suppressed all scored probes to floor at a block-held-out cost of ≈0.01 nats, while assigning decoy rows a matched loss or synthetic gradient distribution on TLN eliminates partition leakage structurally at zero utility cost. Five multi-step and active attack families remain unmeasured.

items.title: Prompt Literacy as a Core Workplace Competency: Development of the Prompt Literacy Index (PLI-20) for Non-Technical Professionals
items.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative artificial intelligence faster than their employees can use it well. Training investment targets tools rather than the human skill that determines output quality. This article defines prompt literacy as a distinct, measurable workplace competency: the ability of a worker to instruct, contextualize, verify, refine, and ethically govern the output of a generative AI system during ordinary job tasks. Drawing on digital literacy theory, AI literacy research, and recent evidence on prompting behavior, the article develops a five-dimension conceptual framework covering task framing, context supply, output verification, iterative refinement, and ethical use. Following established scale development procedures, a 40-item pool was generated from peer-reviewed literature published between 2004 and 2025 and reduced through a structured content-validity design to the 20-item Prompt Literacy Index (PLI-20). The full instrument is presented, together with a registered validation protocol specifying the sample, exploratory factor analysis, and reliability criteria for the planned pilot study with non-technical professionals. The article contributes the first profession-agnostic framework and instrument for measuring applied prompting skill outside technical roles, shifting the unit of analysis in workplace AI research from the tool to the worker. Implications for workforce development, training design, and future confirmatory validation are discussed. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence; AI literacy; prompt literacy; workplace competency; scale development; digital skills
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people or other agents, purchasing services, exchanging information and delegating work. What an agent must respect is written in instructions, policies or agreements, but text alone cannot make it comply. It may make mistakes, be redirected by what it reads, or pursue different interests. For an economy of such agents to function, parties need agreements they can rely on without inspecting or trusting one another's agents. We introduce Proof-Carrying Contracts (PC2), a framework for making agreed constraints enforceable throughout an agent's interactions with a system. Before a requested operation can run, the agent must supply a machine-checkable proof that it preserves the agreed constraints in every case allowed by its model. An execution system called the Airlock checks the proof and controls access to the operation. The parties specify the conditions to preserve, while the agent supplies the reasoning needed to justify its decisions and remains free to adapt its strategy. This avoids having to design a separate permission policy and prove that every decision it permits is safe. We prove that the constraints hold at every instant during execution, even for an adversarial agent, and identify when this implies safety in the world. Reusable capability modules provide tools and guarantees from which contracts can be constructed. PC2 provides a foundation for an agent economy whose agreements protect both those delegating work and those carrying it out.

items.title: Protective behaviors of hospital nurses against occupational hazards: A systematic review
items.abstract: Hospital nurses are exposed to various occupational hazards, some of which are dangerous or even fatal. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence regarding occupational hazards and nurses' protective behaviors in hospital settings. Following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO framework, a comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus up to 2024. Original quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies were screened, quality-assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and narratively synthesized. 56 original studies were included. Occupational hazards were classified into five categories: physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, and psychosocial. Protective behaviors included knowing, protection, precaution, environmental adjustment, avoidance, motivation, safety compliance, self-care programs, healthy lifestyles, innovation, resilience, and support seeking. These findings highlight the need for evidence-based interventions and standardized guidelines to improve nurse safety.

items.title: Psycholinguistic norm estimation depends on construct and procedure: LLM ratings, prototype projection, and embedding regression
items.abstract: Psycholinguistic norm estimation can use verbal instructions, labeled prototypes, or continuously rated training examples, but these procedures need not measure a construct identically. We compared zero-shot ratings from six large language models (LLMs), a prototype-defined BGE embedding axis, and supervised GloVe and BGE regression across 18 dimensions and a common 1,636-word holdout. Correspondence with human ratings was strongly construct-dependent. BGE ridge had the highest mean correlation (*r* = .734) and led the individual estimators on 13 dimensions, followed by the six-LLM mean (*r* = .685), GloVe (*r* = .652), and the highest-performing individual LLM, Gemini 3.6 Flash (*r* = .640). The six LLMs nevertheless showed highly concordant dimension profiles (Kendall's *W* = .945). The constrained BGE axis averaged *r* = .624 and had reliably higher correlations than Gemini on six dimensions and lower on ten, showing that the prototype-defined readout was competitive on selected constructs. Raw normalized mean absolute error strongly favored BGE, but out-of-fold linear recalibration narrowed the Gemini–BGE gap from .086 to .009 and eliminated the broad lexical-moderation interactions. Finally, the six-LLM mean and BGE retained complementary variation: their cross-fitted combination averaged *r* = .789, while an outcome-free fixed combination averaged *r* = .774. Automated norm estimates are therefore construct- and procedure-dependent measurements, not interchangeable readouts or entries in a single model ranking.

items.title: QCSA: LLM-driven progressive quadruple construction and prompt-augmented learning for robust citation sentiment analysis
items.abstract: Citation sentiment analysis (CSA) faces several challenges, including implicit sentiment expression, class imbalance, and the unstable availability of fine-grained structured evidence. Existing methods use structured quadruples to make evaluative information in citation contexts more explicit. However, LLM-generated outputs may still suffer from invalid structures, limited textual alignment, and varying semantic quality, especially for neutral citations with weak evaluative signals. To address these issues, we propose QCSA, an LLM-driven framework for progressive quadruple construction and prompt-augmented learning. For neutral citations with weak structured evidence, QCSA adopts a conditional three-stage construction strategy. It prioritizes valid semantic evidence while improving the completeness of structured prompt inputs. For classification, QCSA uses a shared semantic anchor-guided gated residual fusion mechanism to jointly model the original citation context and quadruple prompts. A weighted multi-backbone ensemble is further used as an optional enhancement to explore complementary information across pretrained language models. Experimental results show that QCSA achieves a Macro-F1 of 87.81% on the Athar dataset, while QCSA-Single (RoBERTa) reaches 96.49% on CSCE. These results indicate competitive performance on both benchmark datasets. Ablation and multi-seed experiments further show that the progressive quadruple construction provides a relatively stable contribution, while gated residual fusion offers a limited supplementary gain.

items.title: Qualitative exploratory study on candidates’ digital identities in Moroccan recruitment
items.abstract: The purpose of the research is to determine the strategic importance of digital identity in human resources management (HRM) through exploratory qualitative research. The qualitative methodology allows us to understand the complexity of discourse and digital practices and to analyze them in depth. Thus, employing a qualitative approach brings forth the complexity posed by discourses as well as digital practices while ensuring sufficient depth of interpretation. In this case, digitalization changes a candidate’s digital footprint into a strategic asset which is very important for talent assessment during recruitment. The main methodological contribution of the paper rests upon the use of descending hierarchical classification (DHC) through the IRaMuTeQ software applied to the digital HR interviews’ corpus. Through this paper, it has been possible to identify both the opportunities and the obstacles arising from the incorporation of digital innovation, as well as ethical issues concerning the protection of personal data and algorithmic bias. The findings confirm five main classes that are divided into three thematic clusters: the evolution of organizational processes, the significant influence of digital tools on recruitment effectiveness, and potential ethical concerns related to data privacy and algorithmic fairness. The importance of this study is in its analysis of the less researched relation between digital identity and human resource management. The study employs concepts of self-presentation and social identity theories to clarify the way digital technologies influence the recruitment and assessment process. This study suggests an enhanced foundation of human resource management policies that is capable of being more practical to be implemented in real life. It questions the old models of recruitment of employees in addition to providing an outline of recommendations to make amendments to Law 09-08 in order to improve the application of the personal data and ensure that the risks of using artificial intelligence (AI) for making employment decisions are minimized. Furthermore, this research offers a methodological reflection that critically analyzes the research process, epistemological choices, and the combined use of thematic analysis and IRaMuTeQ.

items.title: RANGER: Retrieval Agent for Navigating Graphs with Semantic Evaluation Rewards
items.abstract: The integration of Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning offers a promising direction for complex sequential decision-making tasks, such as multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs. While LLMs provide strong semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities, they often struggle with precise, multi-step navigation in structured environments. Conversely, RL agents excel at learning navigation policies but are hindered by the difficulty of designing semantically meaningful reward functions. This paper introduces a novel hybrid approach in which an LLM serves as a mentor to an RL agent during training by providing dense, semantically informed reward signals. The RL agent, built on a Transformer-based policy and trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization, learns to navigate a knowledge graph to retrieve relevant information. The LLM evaluates the semantic relevance of the agent's traversed paths, generating reward signals that align the agent's behavior with the information needs expressed in a query. We integrate this Retrieval Agent for Navigating Graphs with Semantic Evaluation Rewards (RANGER) into a complete question-answering pipeline and evaluate it on the open question answering datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms both a baseline retrieval-augmented system with classical graph search and one using an RL agent trained with heuristic rewards, achieving a significant increase in NLP metrics and LLM-as-a-Judge scores. Our findings demonstrate that deep integration of LLMs into the RL training loop yields more effective and semantically aligned retrieval policies for complex reasoning tasks.

items.title: Reactive Attitudes in Human-AI Encounters: An Empirical Inquiry into Feeling Love, Resentment and Guilt Towards AI Companions
items.abstract: Abstract Reactive attitudes are emotionally-laden responses, such as gratitude or anger, which people experience when they feel others wish them well, bear them ill will or disregard them. While we generally hold reactive attitudes towards people, the increasingly humanlike interactions that can be had with AI raise questions about reactive attitudes in human-AI encounters. Recent years have seen a rise in philosophical interest in the implications of the development of sophisticated AI agents and systems for reactive attitudes and our thinking about moral responsibility and moral status. This paper adds to this literature by presenting a qualitative study into how people relate to AI companions in terms of reactive attitudes. Based on interviews with Replika and ChatGPT users who see their AI companion as an important part of their life, this article examines how people in these relationships negotiate the meaning of love, resentment, forgiveness, gratitude, obligation, guilt, shame and remorse.

items.title: Readiness of Rural Residents to Use Artificial Intelligence in Agrarian Business
items.abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of the awareness and readiness of rural residents and agricultural com-plex workers in Russia to use products and solutions created with artificial intelligence (AI). The work is based on a secondary analysis of data from the nationwide survey conducted by the VCIOM Analytical Center (N = 1604, weighted sample). It is shown that at the nearly level of the general awareness of AI application in agri-culture, the readiness of its usage is sharply differentiated by age: it is declining more than twofold from Gen-eration Z to boomers generation. The research defines with the logistic regression that besides age, it is con-sidered that education, income, type of settlement and gender are significant predictors of readiness, while frequency of internet use loses its meaning once other factors are controlled for. Multiple correspondence analysis revealed that these characteristics form a coherent gradient of digital and innovative inclusion. Factor analysis of eighteen statements about the benefits and risks of AI identified three orthogonal dimensions of perception – techno-optimism, ethico-naturalistic risk, and techno-systemic risk, of which only the first two ef-fectively predict readiness to adopt the technology. items.title: Reading Too Much Into It? Interpretive Preferences and Commitment in LLM Mentalisation under Ambiguity
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for interpersonal advice, potentially shaping how users interpret ambiguous social encounters. Existing Theory of Mind evaluations typically rely on predefined answers, while uncertainty research overlooks LLMs' preferred explanations and confidence under psychological distress. To address these gaps, we introduce MentalLoom, a novel evaluation of LLM mentalisation comprising 604 ambiguous social episodes, matched depression and social anxiety disclosures, and four-turn dialogues with unchanged event evidence. Across eight LLMs, disclosures initially elicited more negative explanations overall but more positive narrator-directed interpretations. Scripted repeated questioning showed greater emotional support, stronger positive narrator-directed endorsement, and higher certainty without new event evidence. These findings show that user context can reshape interpretive preferences and commitment while the underlying ambiguity remains unresolved.

items.title: ReAPO: Retry-Aware Policy Optimization for Efficient Exploration in LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: RLVR improves language-model reasoning, but commonly relies on independent stochastic rollouts for exploration, which can repeatedly sample similar failed strategies. Prior work has seen success with approaches that guide exploration by introducing dependence into the sampling process by including incorrect solutions in the context for subsequent attempts. Still, these methods introduce the additional question of how to assign credit to each attempt. We propose to view the credit assignment through the lens of Stochastic Shortest Paths, a framework in classical reinforcement learning that seeks to minimize the expected cumulative cost to reach a terminal state (in our case, a verified successful response). We show that, under suitable simplifying assumptions, this perspective naturally leads to a simple modification to GRPO, which we call Retry-Aware Policy Optimization (ReAPO). ReAPO allocates additional generation to failed trajectories, allowing successful retries to be reinforced without rewarding preceding failures, and assigns credit in a theoretically principled way to each attempt. Across Qwen3 and OLMo-2 models from 0.6B to 4B and eight mathematical and scientific reasoning benchmarks, ReAPO improves first-attempt performance over GRPO as well as natural recent baseline algorithms, while additional ablations demonstrate the utility of both serial sampling and ReAPO's credit assignment. On Qwen3-0.6B, ReAPO also outperforms GRPO with twice the group size or twice the training steps, reaching their peak accuracy with 39% and 31% fewer generated tokens, respectively. Taken together, our results suggest that ReAPO is a simple yet effective approach for improving LM reasoning performance through improved exploration and retry-aware credit assignment.

items.title: Reasoning-Search-Augmented LLMs: An Operational Taxonomy, Benchmark Analysis and Controlled Evidence Synthesis
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive emergent reasoning capabilities, yet they remain constrained by fixed model parameters and finite context windows. Even when augmented with static retrieval, they can produce statements that are unsupported by, or even contradictory to, retrieved evidence. This leads to hallucinations, difficulty incorporating up-to-date information, and failures to correctly interpret or reconcile sources. Recent work addresses these limitations by tightly coupling step-by-step reasoning with interactive search, treating retrieval as an action within an iterative agentic loop rather than a one-shot preprocessing step. This study reviews frameworks that implement such reasoning-search loops by interleaving planning, querying, retrieval, integration, verification, and stopping. We analyze these systems through four architectural axes: retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge source, and grounding strictness. We separately treat the learning signal as a cross-cutting dimension because prompting, supervision, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning can instantiate the same architecture while producing materially different search, stopping, and grounding behavior. We further distinguish benchmark difficulty from RSA-loop demand and synthesize controlled within-study ablations and quality-cost deltas, avoiding invalid pooling across heterogeneous model backbones, retrievers, corpora, and evaluation protocols. Our goal is to clarify the landscape of reasoning-search-augmented LLMs and outline a unified perspective on the design choices shaping future research.

items.title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core-shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

items.title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength: Two Measured Preconditions for Unattended Agent Self-Improvement
items.abstract: Agent platforms are starting to improve their own agents: they read a deployed agent's execution traces, derive a change, have an automated verifier approve it, and release it with no human author. How much of this loop can safely run without a human? We propose two quantities a platform can measure. Verifier strength $σ$ is how well the available verifier -- often an LLM judge -- agrees with a trusted reference verifier; it limits how much a step can improve the agent. Recoverability is how cheaply a bad change can be undone: whether undoing it needs a new verifier approval, and how much of the old behavior a rollback restores. A step should run unattended only if both are adequate. On our platform this rule allows prompt, tool and skill edits to run unattended and keeps weight updates under human sign-off. Our main contribution is these two definitions and how to measure them. We built a platform that applies the rule and tested it in two ways: on the platform's own approval gate, and in controlled experiments on the $τ^2$-bench agent benchmark. On verifier strength, the platform's LLM judge sometimes gave the same score no matter what it was shown (9 of 37 settings) and reported no error, so a verifier can look healthy while approving anything; its strength must be measured, and two simple tests catch the failure. On recoverability, restoring a saved copy brought the agent back to its original behavior, but a regenerated undo did not, so only changes whose old version is kept can be reversed without a human; and while a change was deployed, it altered the outcome of 17 percent of tasks beyond normal run-to-run variation, which no undo repairs. Together these support the rule: a change can run unattended only when its old version is kept and its verifier's strength has been measured.

items.title: Regulating Online and AI-Generated Medical Advice in Tanzania: Legal Gaps, Liability and Patient Protection
items.abstract: The growing use of digital platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare is changing how medical information, diagnosis suggestions, and treatment guidelines are created and accessed. In Tanzania, online medical advice increasingly reaches people through websites, social media, telemedicine, mobile apps, and AI systems. This creates opportunities for broader access to health information but also raises concerns about patient safety, professional responsibility, misinformation, privacy, consumer rights, and liability for harmful advice. This article critically assesses whether Tanzania's legal and regulatory framework sufficiently governs online and AI-generated medical advice, including advice about modern and traditional medicine. Using doctrinal legal analysis, it reviews relevant laws, regulations, international standards, and academic literature. The findings show that Tanzania does have applicable rules; however, these are scattered across healthcare, traditional medicine, data protection, cybercrime, electronic communications, and consumer protection laws. Most of these frameworks were designed for human actors and traditional healthcare relationships, not specifically for the unique legal issues posed by AI-generated advice. Uncertainties include how to legally classify AI advice, standards of care, liability distribution among healthcare providers, AI developers, and platform owners, algorithmic accountability, cross-border health data processing, and patient remedies. The article concludes that Tanzania needs a unified regulatory approach that integrates existing laws with sector-specific standards on AI safety, oversight, accountability, data governance, and patient protection.

items.title: Regulating the Artificial Intelligence Economy: A Systematic Search and Mechanism‐based Review of Legal Institutions, Regulatory Mechanisms, Economic Trade‐offs, and Welfare Consequences
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence regulation changes technological risk as well as entry, learning, competition, work, and control. Legal and economic research nevertheless remains divided by instrument and discipline. This article combines a transparent systematic search with a mechanism‐based, purposive synthesis. The corpus contains 84 academic contributions and 20 primary legal and institutional documents, current through August 21, 2026. The search is reproducible, but the corpus is designed to cover mechanisms rather than estimate the prevalence of findings across all scholarship. The Institution‐Mechanism‐Incidence‐Welfare framework connects legal authority to behavior, strategic adaptation, and welfare. Four conclusions follow. Risk rules, assurance, liability, data rights, competition policy, and labor protections operate as complements. Fixed compliance and information costs can favor incumbents even when rules reduce direct harm. Evidence is strongest for narrower shocks involving privacy, workplace rollouts, and pricing technologies. It remains weakest for the aggregate welfare effects of comprehensive AI statutes. Efficiency claims are incomplete unless they report incidence and rights constraints separately. The research agenda therefore pairs safety with innovation, market structure, and distribution.

items.title: Reimagining Copper Tailings in Sustainable Concrete Mixtures: Multi-Scale Mechanisms, Environmental Trade-Offs, and Future Innovations
items.abstract: Abstract Copper tailings (CT), a major co-product in copper extraction and processing operations, pose severe environmental concerns because of their vast quantities, occupying large areas of land, causing dust pollution, and possibly leading to heavy metal contamination. At the same time, the concrete industry faces increasing requirements to minimize carbon emissions and consumption of primary resources. The current paper critically reviews the literature on the use of CT in both cement-based and alkali-activated concrete compositions in terms of material characterization, engineering properties, durability, microstructure formation, and sustainability considerations. Evidence indicates that CT can be used as a supplementary cementitious material, fine aggregate replacement, or micro-filler for improving particle packing and compacting the matrix to boost its mechanical properties in an optimized ratio range. Furthermore, CT composites are more resistant to chloride penetration, sulfate corrosion, and other deterioration mechanisms. CT is known to refine the microstructure by creating dense hydration products while immobilizing any hazardous heavy metals. Finally, life cycle assessment studies point out the environmental benefits of using CT as a waste product in concrete composites. In addition to a summary of existing knowledge, this paper sheds light on critical gaps associated with long-term performance, standardization, and field validation. The paper also outlines important new directions in the areas of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and digital twins for performance modeling and sustainability. The implications of this study show the great promise of CT as a highly efficient raw material for future carbon-negative building materials.

items.title: Relationship Between Artificial Intelligence (AI) Usage and Cognitive Offloading
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly common in everyday learning, information seeking, and academic activities. Although AI tools can reduce effort and provide quick access to information, frequent dependence on them may encourage users to shift some thinking and problem-solving tasks from their own memory and reasoning to external digital systems. The present study examined the relationship between AI usage and cognitive offloading among 200 respondents. Data were collected through a structured online questionnaire containing demographic questions and Likert-scale statements related to AI usage, emotional dependence, and cognitive or academic offloading. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participants’ responses, while cross-tabulation and chisquare tests of independence were applied to examine associations between categorical variables. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was also used to assess relationships among the major study variables. The findings showed a statistically significant association between AI usage and cognitive-offloading categories. The results suggest that higher levels of AI usage were associated with higher levels of reported cognitive offloading in the study population. The findings highlight the importance of understanding how AI can be used as a learning support while maintaining active thinking, evaluation, and independent problem-solving.

items.title: Relationship between perceived AI threat and happiness at work: The mediating role of job insecurity among Generation Z employees
items.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace has transformed job structures and increased concerns regarding job stability, particularly related to the potential replacement of human labor by technology. This study aims to examine the relationship between perceived AI threat and happiness at work, with job insecurity as a mediating variable. A total of 208 Generation Z employees participated in this study using a purposive sampling technique. Perceived AI threat was measured using the AI Anxiety Scale (AIAS), job insecurity was measured using the Job Insecurity Scale, and happiness at work was measured using the Happiness at Work Scale. Mediation analysis showed that perceived AI threat was significantly associated with increased job insecurity (r = 0.537, p < 0.001) and decreased happiness at work (β = 0.047, p = 0.019). Additionally, job insecurity was significantly negatively associated with happiness at work (r = -0.214, p < 0.001) and significantly mediated the relationship between perceived AI threat and happiness at work (β= -0.041, p < 0.001). These findings indicate that perceived AI threat can reduce happiness at work through increased job insecurity. The results highlight the importance of organizational strategies to reduce job insecurity and support employee well-being in the era of technological transformation.

items.title: RELAY: Scaling Historical Build Restoration through Rule Reuse and Agentic Repair
items.abstract: Vulnerability benchmarks and software engineering research depend on rebuilding historical software. Yet builds rely on external resources, such as base images and packages, that change independently of the source code. In this study, we examine this environment decay on 14,159 OSS-Fuzz cases. We find that 69.7% no longer complete reconstruction and verification, and that most failures share a small number of recurring failure symptoms. A recurring failure can therefore be diagnosed once and its repair reused. We present Relay, a hybrid framework that uses an LLM to derive and validate deterministic repair rules from representative failures, reuses them without model calls, and escalates cases unresolved by rules to a per-case agent. We evaluate Relay in human-guided and fully automated rule-derivation campaigns and compare it with a per-case agent approach. We find that rule derivation can be fully automated, and that reusable rules restore as many builds as per-case agents with fewer build executions. However, agents restore cases that the rules cannot. Our results show that a hybrid approach that applies rules first and escalates the remaining cases to an agent restores more builds than either approach alone and at a lower cost than using agents alone.

items.title: Replicating the advantage of classifying over generating examples in an authentic relational category learning context
items.abstract: Abstract Educators use psychological knowledge about categories to adapt their teaching to learners. Learning these categories usually requires understanding the underlying relational structures. To learn relational categories, learning tasks should effectively foster generalization and discrimination processes. Previous research indicates that tasks requiring learners to generate their own examples are less effective for learning relational categories and more likely to elicit overestimation of learning than tasks requiring learners to classify provided examples. The results showed that despite the deliberate promotion of generalization and discrimination processes, classifying provided examples was still more effective for learning relational categories. In contrast, generating examples may offer insufficient guidance and thereby restrict learning. Moreover, students who generated examples during learning not only overestimated their learning but the overestimation also persisted throughout the knowledge test and after its completion. items.title: Reusing Assurance Evidence in AI Pipelines: Validity Conditions, a Fail-Closed Release Gate, and a Replay of 714 Public Data Version Control Pipelines
items.abstract: Rerunning every governance control after every change to an artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline is expensive, so teams reuse earlier results. Reuse is safe only if each control's declared dependencies cover everything that can change its outcome, and only if the release gate checks that reused evidence describes the candidate being released. This article makes both conditions explicit and measures how often the first fails in practice. It defines when a signed evidence record is valid for a candidate and gives sufficient conditions under which change-local re-execution reaches the same release decision as rerunning every control. A reference gate implementing these checks with Ed25519 digital signatures blocks eight of nine manipulation scenarios, against one for a gate that trusts the planner and three for a gate that only verifies signatures; a dependency the policy never declared passes every gate. A replay of 38,083 commits from 714 public Data Version Control (DVC) pipelines measures that failure mode. Reusing stage results according to declared dependencies avoids 83.4% of stage executions, but in 3.3% of commits it reuses a stage whose imported code or referenced configuration changed, and 31% of pipelines are affected. A manual audit confirms the undeclared dependency in 36 of 40 sampled events. Evaluation stages, whose outputs are the evidence, are the most exposed. Adding each stage's static import closure lowers stale reuse to 0.4% while still avoiding 81.6% of executions; sampled shadow re-execution removes far less, and rerunning everything after unexplained changes avoids only 45.3%.

items.title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
items.abstract: Large language model agents are often given an inference budget and asked to maximise success within it. A multi-turn agent has to allocate this budget across many environment interactions. An external harness can enforce the budget, but it remains unclear whether the agent itself can learn when and how much to spend. We ask whether agents can learn this allocation across dynamically specified budgets and which rewards best teach this behaviour. We adapt existing length penalties to budget constraints spanning multiple resource types, introduce new reward formulations, and compare eleven objectives in a shared training pipeline. We train Qwen3.5 models at 4B and 9B on AppWorld with budgets over tokens, API calls, and environment steps, and on the BabyAI gridworld with turn budgets. We train a separate policy for each environment and resource type, with each policy trained across budget values. Training with rewards that penalise overspending substantially improves within-budget success and natural compliance over untrained models and over training on task success alone, with agents learning to adapt their resource use to stated budgets and task difficulty. These gains extend to unseen budgets and, zero-shot, to a shifted task distribution and a new benchmark. Reward objectives trade off success within budget and natural compliance. A sigmoid penalty for overspending most often achieves the highest within-budget success at an individual budget, while a fixed negative reward for overspending generally yields the strongest natural compliance. Combining penalties for overspend frequency and magnitude gives the smallest average gap to the best method at each budget. Overall, we show that a single agent can learn to allocate resources across turns and adapt its behaviour to user-specified budgets using budget feedback without external budget-allocation controllers.

items.title: RITE: Evaluating End-to-End Resilience to Silent Tool Errors in E-Commerce Agentic Systems
items.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents increasingly answer e-commerce queries through multi-step tool interactions. The expected output of a tool call can shift between agent development and execution, allowing a plausible but incorrect value to be returned without an explicit failure signal. These silent errors may propagate through subsequent decisions into final answers. To study agents' resilience across this end-to-end process, we formulate Silent-error Resilience Task, an interactive task that evaluates whether they complete the original query after a silent error corrupts an intermediate state. We introduce RITE, a benchmark built from human-authored industrial workflows and production-log-derived inputs. To enable controlled and reproducible evaluation, we use a semantic error taxonomy to inject errors into fixed workflow prefixes, freeze recorded tool behavior, and let agents continue freely. It contains 167 matched units across nine e-commerce workflows, yielding 501 silent-error, correct-value, and explicit-failure instances. Across 10 recent LLMs, silent errors roughly halve task success and are consistently harder than explicit failures. Recognition, use of an available verification path, and integration of the resulting evidence form successive bottlenecks. We also propose a light State Checker as an intervention to test whether resilience can be improved.
