items.title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
items.abstract: Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.

items.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
items.abstract: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should. A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation. We study this risk through the lens of AI control. We introduce RSI Control Arena, a testbed in which a frontier model, acting as an autonomous R\&D agent, is given a benign main task from a stage of a successor model's training pipeline together with a covert side task to install a misaligned property in the successor. The testbed contains 16 side tasks in three classes, forming 22 task pairs with main tasks that span the pipeline from data curation to reinforcement learning. We evaluate six frontier models as agents against LLM monitors that read the transcript of the run and the agent's reasoning. We observe that every model completes a substantial share of the side tasks without degrading the main-task performance, including side tasks that make the successor itself a better saboteur. Under minimal instructions to stay covert, models already produce successful attacks that monitors fail to detect, and providing a short list of evasion tactics further reduces the detection rate. Monitors with access to agent's reasoning detects most attacks, but not all. Our results indicate that recursive self-improvement raises significant safety concerns, and that strong safety effort should be in place before models are trusted with greater responsibility of training their successors.

items.title: SAGE-HAP: Sustainability-Certified Agentic Communication and Computing at a Solar-Powered High-Altitude Platform
items.abstract: The solar-powered High-Altitude Platforms (HAP) can provide persistent communication and computing services beyond terrestrial coverage. However, changing mission priorities, coupled resource demands, and uncertain solar supply complicate sustainable scheduling, while large language model proposals require independent feasibility checks. This paper proposes SAGE, a Sustainability-certified Agentic Ground-service Engine for a HAP. We formulate an energy-causal stochastic optimization problem incorporating semantic modes, multi-user interference, channel aging, essential platform loads, and battery stress. An agent translates operator intent into typed admission, mode, and grouping candidates, while deterministic convex refinement and an action shield verify resource and reserve feasibility using calibrated solar lower bounds before execution. Agent proposals and deterministic fallbacks share the same certification path. Residual-based forecasting and memory-assisted replanning close the control loop. We establish fixed-candidate convexity, reserve safety under calibrated solar coverage and bounded actuation error, and an online utility bound accounting for candidate-generation error. At nominal load, simulations show 2.38 percentage points higher completion and 5.27% greater useful-workload energy efficiency than energy-harvesting Lyapunov control. Under stressed load and solar uncertainty, reserve violations occur in 1/50 runs, versus 47/50 without energy certification. A 600-record calibrated inference replay further shows 23.5--36.5% utility gains over deterministic-only candidates under compound stress.

items.title: SANE: Automated Scorer-Specific Metamorphic Testing for LLM Judges
items.abstract: LLM judges increasingly mediate benchmark evaluation, model selection, data curation, and training. Their decisions are useful only when each judge responds reliably to changes affecting its scoring criterion. Existing methods for reliability testing perturb inputs with known expected effects on judge scores. Prominent LLM-judge testing harnesses combine human-authored perturbation recipes with synthetic test generation, leaving scorer-specific recipe ideation outside the automated pipeline. This limits their use to fixed perturbations and pre-assumed scorer types. We introduce SANE, an agent-based framework that encodes behavioral requirements for stochastic evaluators as reusable agent instructions. Given a scorer specification, implementation, and representative inputs, the pipeline first identifies scorer-specific capabilities, then automatically derives perturbation recipes and expected score relations for each. SANE also defines a scorer-independent validation framework for generated judge tests. It determines whether each recipe agrees with scorer intent and whether each instantiated case realizes the recipe and supports its expected relation. Because SANE generates a recipe inventory tailored to each scorer, the number of aligned recipes grows as scorers are added. Across five domains, SANE produces 3.7 times as many validated test families as the Judge Reliability Harness (JRH) at comparable end-to-end validity and detects scorer deficiencies in every domain, including professionalism and toxicity, where JRH detects none. On faithfulness, SANE achieves strong human alignment in judge ranking: its test-suite scores rank 11 judge models consistently with human-labeled FaithBench performance (Spearman rho = 0.852), while JRH does not (rho = 0.100).

items.title: SAPD: Learning from Agent Experience without Environment Interaction
items.abstract: Scaling the training of Large Language Model (LLM) agents typically requires a large collection of executable environments, whose construction, maintenance, and operation constrain the expansion of training experience. Existing offline trajectories offer an opportunity to reuse interaction experience, yet effectively refining the current policy without revisiting these environments remains challenging: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can lead to catastrophic forgetting, while online reinforcement learning requires real-time interaction with the environment. To address this challenge, we propose Step-Advantage Policy Distillation (SAPD), a method for learning from offline trajectories using relative step advantages. SAPD decomposes multi-turn trajectories into individual decision contexts for on-policy distillation, allowing the student to generate responses conditioned on recorded histories, and introduces relative step advantage signals to stabilize training. The entire process requires neither new environment observations nor additional multi-turn interactions. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-based QA show that SAPD improves performance across different teacher configurations, mitigates catastrophic forgetting compared with SFT, and runs at least $4.7\times$ faster per training step than online OPD. We will release our code soon.

items.title: Scaling Therapy Supervision: Assessing Psychotherapy Fidelity Using Large Language Models
items.abstract: Psychotherapy fidelity assessment measures how faithfully a therapist adheres to a treatment protocol, a critical determinant of positive patient outcomes. However, fidelity assessment is bottlenecked by manual expert review, rendering the process labor-intensive and unscalable. To scale therapy supervision and support clinician self-learning, we present an integrated application of large language models (LLMs) that automates psychotherapy fidelity workflows and generates actionable supervisory feedback from authentic, long-form clinical transcripts. We evaluate three open-weight models across multiple task decomposition configurations and reasoning strategies, demonstrating that evidence-first reasoning improves fidelity estimation. Furthermore, we establish the framework's external construct validity on an independent randomized controlled trial (RCT), where it reliably distinguishes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) from non-CBT sessions across core therapeutic skills. Through a user study that evaluates the generated feedback, mental health experts indicate that the pipeline synthesizes actionable clinical feedback. Ultimately, our work offers a practical, scalable solution toward bridging the community mental health supervision gap.

A companion short demonstration paper describes Scriptorium's interaction design; because a demonstration format is constrained to a few pages, it necessarily omits most implementation detail. This report documents Scriptorium's complete system architecture, data model, collaborative-interaction design rationale, and AI orchestration mechanism, including verbatim agent prompts, the deterministic guardrails that constrain them, the language model and retrieval configuration, and the steps needed to run the system, so that the design can be inspected, critiqued, reproduced, and reused by other researchers. We also discuss the system's current limitations and the user study we are planning to evaluate its central hypothesis: that combining collaborative transparency with scoped multi-agent AI assistance increases serendipitous cross-pollination between collaborators' research threads.

items.title: SecureFlow: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Automated Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection and Patching
items.abstract: Smart contracts govern substantial financial value on public blockchains; however, because deployed contract code is immutable, a vulnerability that survives review cannot be patched in place. Pre-deployment auditing is the main safeguard for contract security; in addition to providing a warning, it must identify the flaw, explain why it is exploitable, and supply a candidate correction. Static analyzers match fixed patterns and emit many false alarms, while a single large language model asked to detect, explain, and repair a flaw in one pass tends to degrade on each subtask. We introduce SecureFlow, a multi-agent framework in which three agents share a Qwen3-8B backbone: SecureProbe detects vulnerable contracts, SecureAnalyze classifies them under the DASP Top-10, and SecureSynthesize writes a root-cause explanation and a minimally invasive patch through in-context learning. Against seventeen open and proprietary models on the SmartBug and Smart Contract Vulnerability datasets, SecureFlow performs on par with the strongest baselines, including fine-tuned GPT-4o, reaching accuracy and weighted F1 of 0.93 and 0.96 on the two datasets, respectively, while running locally on 8B open weights. It completes reports for 93.33% and 85.15% of instances; in blinded manual review of 50 sampled completed reports per dataset, patch and explanation validity are respectively 0.94 and 0.96 on SmartBug and 0.88 and 0.90 on the second dataset. A controlled prompt study shows that adding the predicted label and a knowledge-base hint improves generation and validity for every model, making prompt design a primary factor for language model auditing. An end-to-end auditor can match proprietary baselines while explaining and repairing flaws.

items.title: Seeing inside the black box: Effects of algorithmic knowledge on system trustworthiness in aviation
items.abstract: Automation has shaped aircraft design for the past seven decades, moving from fully manual control to highly automated systems. Despite this, pilots retain final authority for safety-critical decisions, which requires continuous trust calibration. This study investigated how algorithmic transparency influences pilots' learned trust in an AI-based cockpit assistant. Twenty-one commercial pilots were randomly assigned to an early transparency condition (detailed explanations of the AI's algorithms and performance provided before the tutorial) or a late transparency condition (the same information delivered after the experiment). Each pilot used the assistant during a tutorial and a realistic simulated flight. Mixed-effects ordinal models showed higher trust ratings for the early compared to the late transparency group during both tutorial and flight, and a larger trust increase between phases. In conclusion, providing pilots with timely, clear information about AI processes modestly improves trust and supports calibrated reliance.

items.title: Self-Evolving Static Analysis via LLM Pseudo-Labeling
items.abstract: Security bugs often slip past static analysis not because they are impossible to detect, but because detection rules have not yet been written for the code in front of us. New frameworks, APIs, and coding idioms continually create such gaps, leaving developers to discover failures and manually encode new rules. We present SESAA, a framework in which an Large Language Model (LLM) agent starts from no rules and iteratively evolves a set of readable and auditable joern queries. The agent receives feedback only from a second LLM critic, which inspects flagged and unflagged code to identify likely false alarms and suspected misses, without access to ground-truth labels. The agent then uses this feedback to revise its queries. On the OWASP Benchmark for Python, SESAA reaches a mean F1 of 0.742 across 8 independent runs, well above the default configurations of five widely used tools and comparable to the strongest of them once it is tuned with access to ground-truth labels that SESAA never sees. In a pilot on real-world Python projects, queries induced from code available before a vulnerability was introduced detect 10 of 19 subsequent CVEs, including 9 detected by rules written for the same repository. The resulting detector is a set of executable, human-readable queries that engineers can inspect, modify, and run independently. These results suggest that LLM agents can turn static-analysis rule maintenance from a manually authored process into an iterative process of automated discovery and repair.

items.title: Self-Healing AI-Enhanced Web Applications: A Runtime Observability and Recovery Framework
items.abstract: Intelligent web applications increasingly depend on artificial intelligence for personalization, retrieval, natural-language interaction and task automation. These capabilities improve user experience but also introduce new runtime failures, including model uncertainty, stale context, broken user interface states, failed tool calls and inconsistent data flows. This paper proposes a Self-Healing AI-Enhanced Web Application framework that combines runtime telemetry, failure classification, policy-constrained repair planning and human review. The framework treats recovery as a controlled application workflow rather than an unrestricted model action. It identifies failure classes, ranks low-risk repair strategies such as retry, rollback, revalidation and alternate path selection, and escalates high-risk changes for human approval. The contribution is a reference architecture, an operational workflow and an evaluation protocol for measuring recovery quality, user impact, safety and auditability. The paper argues that future intelligent web applications should be judged not only by initial task success but also by their ability to detect, explain and recover from failures without losing user trust.

items.title: Semantic enrichment and dynamic refinement: prototype-guided remote sensing image segmentation
items.abstract: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing imagery is a pivotal task in computer vision. Despite remarkable progress driven by deep learning—particularly convolutional neural networks and Transformers—existing methods still struggle with complex backgrounds, multiscale targets, and limited annotated data, leading to suboptimal performance for small objects and fine-grained categories. To address these challenges, we propose ProtoFiNet, a semantic segmentation model that integrates prototype learning with foundation-model knowledge to enhance feature representation and segmentation accuracy. Unlike conventional approaches relying on randomly initialized prototypes, ProtoFiNet enriches prototypes with semantic information from the pretrained Scale-MAE model, fine-tuned via low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for efficient adaptation to remote sensing scenarios. The model incorporates a contextual prototype refinement branch for dynamic prototype updating, coupled with two loss functions—prototype disentanglement optimization and prototype compactness contrastive loss—to enhance intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Here, we show that ProtoFiNet achieves state-of-the-art performance across three benchmark datasets: ISPRS Vaihingen (mIoU=84.68%), ISPRS Potsdam (mIoU=87.64%), and LoveDA (mIoU=52.81%), outperforming existing methods by 1.56% to 3.1% in mIoU. These results highlight the model’s effectiveness in segmenting small targets and complex backgrounds.

items.title: Semantic Knowledge Graph Framework for Assessing Flood-Induced Traffic Risk from Social Media Data
items.abstract: With the intensification of global climate change, extreme precipitation events have become more frequent and intense, underscoring the need for rapid collection and accurate analysis of disaster information to improve emergency response efficiency. Social media, as a rich source of unstruc-tured, high-frequency, and near-real-time data, holds significant potential for urban disaster monitoring and assessment. However, its utility is limited by noise, semantic redundancy, and loosely structured content, which hinder the accurate extraction and structured representation of disaster information. To address the rapid assessment of flood-related road traffic impacts during urban pluvial flooding, this study proposes a social-media-driven framework for constructing a hierarchical semantic knowledge graph of flood-related road impacts. Using flood-related social media data collected from Weibo and road network data from OpenStreetMap (OSM), the pro-posed framework integrates text deduplication, road and geographic information extraction, Transformer-based impact severity classification, and knowledge graph construction. First, a deduplication approach combining MinHash-LSH candidate filtering with embedding-based se-mantic similarity verification is applied to remove redundant social media posts, followed by the extraction of flood-related road and geographic information from the retained texts. Second, a Transformer-based text classification model classifies the extracted road-related information into four flood-related impact severity levels. Finally, a dictionary- and rule-constrained entity extrac-tion approach is used to construct a hierarchical semantic knowledge graph encompassing spatial locations, entity relationships, and impact severity attributes. The extracted road entities are fur-ther matched to the OSM road network to enable spatial representation of the identified impacts. The experimental results show that the proposed deduplication method achieved an accuracy of 94.1%, outperforming standalone MinHash, SimHash, and embedding-based methods. The Transformer model achieved precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy of 0.97, 0.98, 0.97, and 0.97, respectively, and outperformed the evaluated traditional machine-learning and RNN-based models. Furthermore, the proposed framework successfully transformed fragmented and un-structured social media information into structured and georeferenced road-impact information by linking affected road entities with spatial locations and flood-related impact severity attributes. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework to support rapid identification of flood-related road impacts, disaster situational awareness, and emergency transportation man-agement.

items.abstract: Introduction Musculoskeletal disorders associated with muscular strain on the neck and shoulders affect women in administration more often than men. Ergonomic guidelines have historically been derived from male models, often ignoring biomechanical differences between the sexes. This study aims to quantify the acute mechanical response of the neck muscles of men and women to a standardized writing task at university desks of the same height and 0° inclination. METHODS: The research involved 57 healthy university students (34 women, 23 men; age 19-24 years). Muscle tone (F), stiffness (S), and viscoelastic decrement (D) in the sternocleidomastoideus muscle (SCM), trapezius muscle (UT), and semispinalis capitis muscle (SSC) were assessed by the non-invasive MyotonPRO device before and after 20 min of continuous writing. RESULTS: = 0.039). On average, SCM tone increased slightly in men (+0.120 Hz) and decreased in women (-0.294 Hz), while SSC tone decreased in men (-0.374 Hz) and increased in women (+0.450 Hz). CONCLUSIONS: A twenty-minute writing task at a university desk with a fixed height was associated with measurable acute changes in selected mechanical properties of the neck muscles and with differences between the sexes in the direction of change in the tone of SCM and SSC. The clinical relevance of these findings remains unclear and should be validated in larger studies with detailed anthropometric and ergonomic evaluation and longer follow-up.

items.title: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
items.abstract: When training LLMs to code with reinforcement learning, reward hacking is often detectable but difficult to prevent, since (a) environment hardening is increasingly difficult as training environments grow more complex; and (b) training-time interventions incentivize models to obfuscate hacking behavior to bypass detection. We instead study whether we can predict when detectable reward hacking becomes dominant before executing an RL run, enabling us to select lower-risk recipes in advance. We find that the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset, which varies substantially across training recipes and repeated runs. We thus formulate this problem as predicting the distribution of the reward hacking onset step under a target training recipe. We introduce SimHack, a simulator that learns reward hacking training dynamics from a handful of smaller-scale reference RL runs and generates counterfactual simulation runs of unseen target recipes without costly retraining. Across unseen target recipes, SimHack predicts the median onset to a relative error of 11.3% and achieves across-recipe rank correlation of 0.85, while generalizing to differences in model scale, curriculum, number of rollouts, and learning rate between reference and target recipes. As an application, we show that SimHack can guide training decisions by screening candidate RL curricula, discovering curricula over the same set of scenarios that train for 96.6% longer without hacking.

items.title: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models
items.abstract: Current evaluation of LLMs on benchmarks typically aggregates performance over individual examples into a single scalar score. This approach is overly coarse and ignores the diverse scope of skills covered by benchmark datasets. To address this limitation and better exploit benchmark data, we propose SkillEval, a new evaluation framework that performs cross-model, skill-level analysis. The framework integrates advances from two areas: (1) it leverages the meta-cognitive capabilities of LLMs to automatically discover interpretable skills from questions, and (2) it applies cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) from psychometrics to estimate per-skill abilities of LLMs. We conduct experiments on 3,811 LLMs evaluated on 9,523 items across five benchmarks spanning diverse domains (MATH, BBH, GPQA, MuSR, IFEval). Compared to the traditional average-based evaluation paradigm, SkillEval produces reliable, more calibrated and informative yet concise model profiles that more accurately predict model behavior on unseen items. We also demonstrate the utility of SkillEval in two downstream tasks: (1) LLM routing, which dynamically assigns each query to a capable but efficient model, reducing inference cost by over 60% while achieving improved performance, and (2) Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT), where an unseen model can be efficiently evaluated using a trained CDM. Furthermore, we show that these skill profiles provide useful insights, for example, how benchmarks share skills and how instruction-tuned models differ from their base models.

items.title: SLoSa: Small, Low-Power, and Safe Foundation Models for Robotic Task Planning
items.abstract: Safe robotic task planning requires planners that can reliably achieve task goals while satisfying safety constraints. Classical planners search over explicit symbolic task representations and can provide formal guarantees with respect to encoded safety constraints, but require rigid input formats. Their computational cost also increases rapidly with the search space. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) offer flexible task interfaces and strong generalization capabilities, but they are large, power-hungry, and pre-trained with little robot-specific safety data and knowledge. Thus, they can be difficult to deploy locally on robotic systems with limited resources. To address these limitations, we present SLoSa, a neuro-symbolic compression and fine-tuning framework for training foundation-model-based robotic task planners with Small size, Low power demand, and Safety awareness. The framework first constructs a safety-aware dataset using classical planners, an advanced teacher LLM, and formal verifiers, followed by two training stages: supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning guided by a verification-based reward machine to enforce safety alignment. We evaluate SLoSa across four Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) domains, two household simulation environments, local edge platforms, and a desktop robotic arm. Across the PDDL tasks, verifier-guided post-training raises the success rate of compact 4B-14B planners to 70.5-76.0%, while INT4 deployment on a Jetson Orin requires 17.85-26.41 W of average power. Results in household simulators and on the physical robot further demonstrate the applicability of SLoSa across diverse robotic task settings.

items.title: SMART: Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics
items.abstract: Word error rate (WER) assigns equal cost to lexical edits despite their different semantic consequences, while overall semantic scores cannot identify which individual errors alter the intended meaning. We formulate ASR semantic evaluation as context-aware, segment-level consequence assessment and propose Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics (SMART), a framework for traceable semantic evaluation and targeted ASR correction. SMART maps reference-hypothesis discrepancies into coherent segments and applies a structured contextual rubric to assign explicit consequence labels. These labels support Semantic Impact Error Rate (SIER), which quantifies consequential errors at utterance, chunk, and lexical levels. Against majority-vote human labels, SMART achieves 0.843 F1 versus 0.745 for direct LLM judgment. Evaluation across multiple LLMs further demonstrates that SMART is relatively insensitive to the choice of evaluation model, while MER and SIER reveal different aspects of ASR quality. A separate target-reference-free rubric guides correction using the target hypothesis and surrounding ASR hypotheses, outperforming a matched w/o Rubric baseline on both datasets, with further absolute reductions of 0.85-0.98 percentage points in MER and 1.18-1.65 percentage points in SIER_lex.

items.title: Social Media Marketing, Digital Retail Media Advertising, and Generative AI: A Systematic Review of Their Impact on Consumer Engagement and Purchase Behaviour
items.abstract: This research systematically examines the impact of digital retail media advertising, social media marketing, and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) on consumer engagement, brand loyalty, and purchasing decisions within the retail sector. Using a systematic literature review under the PRISMA framework, 25 peer-reviewed articles were thematically analyzed to distill the trends and gaps. Findings show that personalized digital retail advertising enhances customer conversion, while social media fosters brand loyalty through network dynamics and peer influence. However, challenges like privacy concerns, ad fatigue, and GenAI’s lack of emotional authenticity were also evident. The study contributes to theoretical models such as the Hierarchy of Effects, Network Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model by suggesting necessary updates for the digital era. Practical recommendations for retailers include investing in data-driven personalization, maintaining ethical transparency, and balancing automation with human interaction. This research underscores the increasing necessity for ethical marketing practices in a rapidly transforming digital landscape and offers insights for future academic exploration and strategic business development focused on sustaining consumer trust and engagement.

items.title: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.abstract: Cellular states are shaped by both intrinsic gene expression programs and the spatial microenvironment in which cells reside. Spatial transcriptomics makes this context measurable, but effective representation learning requires capturing both spatially informative molecular signals and intercellular organization. Existing approaches address these challenges only partially: conventional gene selection can overlook spatially structured signals, while methods for encoding cell-cell relationships often either reduce a cell's microenvironment to proximity alone, discarding direction, or rely on absolute coordinates tied to an arbitrary tissue frame. Consequently, cells with similar neighbor distances but distinct spatial organization may receive overly similar representations, despite experiencing different biological contexts that shape their cellular states. We introduce Tessera, a spatial representation learning framework that addresses both molecular selection and cellular context. Tessera combines spatially informed gene selection with a geometric inductive bias that contextualizes each cell within its local tissue environment. By modeling relative cell-cell relationships, Tessera is translation-invariant while preserving direction, allowing neighboring cells to contribute differently according to their spatial context and cellular state. Across held-out tissues and technologies, Tessera outperforms existing spatial foundation models in representation quality and generalizes zero-shot to contexts up to $16\times$ larger than those seen during training.

items.title: Speak vs. Know: Balancing Behavior and Knowledge Distributions of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Recent work reports that the distribution verbalized directly in the output text aligns far better with human opinion distributions than the next-token log-probability distribution of LLMs. However, the verbalized distribution reflects what LLMs know about a group's opinions (knowledge distribution), while what they actually output at deployment is governed by their log-probability distribution (behavior distribution). We find that when prompting LLMs to predict the opinion of a specific group, the most likely answer under the verbalized distribution differs from that under the log-probability distribution for 37% of World Values Survey questions, averaged over three LLMs. Thus, LLMs' knowledge does not match their behavior. This matters for evaluation: a verbalized distribution can score well against a group while its most likely answer is one the model never outputs, so the score no longer describes the model. The alignment scores for these two distributions reflect only the model's behavior or its knowledge, separately. We therefore propose a learnable combination of the two distributions that follows the most likely answer of the behavior distribution while preserving the shape of the knowledge distribution, with a single hyperparameter trading off behavioral fidelity against distribution quality. Our experiments on three opinion survey datasets and six models show that the balanced distribution improves behavioral consistency over the verbalized distribution from 71.6% to 95.6% on average, while the total variation distance to the human opinion distributions rises only slightly from 28.8% to 33.8%, and it remains effective under temperature scaling and cross-dataset settings.

items.title: Speech2Pro: Speech-driven in-situ projection authoring for stage performance
items.abstract: Intelligent projection plays an important role in stage performances, yet in-situ projection authoring remains time-consuming and difficult to adapt to dynamic physical conditions. We use projection authoring to refer to the workflow of translating creative intent into visual content, grounding it in the physical scene, inspecting projected outcomes, and refining the result; image generation is only one step in this workflow. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) offers opportunities to support this workflow, but applying general-purpose models in situ raises interaction challenges of robustness, alignment, and control. We examine speech-driven in-situ projection authoring as an interaction design problem and present Speech2Pro, a prototype that integrates speech input, generative image models, and depth-aware scene sensing to mediate between user intent, generated content, and physical context. Its enabling mechanism, Contrastive Learning Integrated with Perception Data Fusion (CLIPF), combines contrastive training with depth-aware inference to reduce breakdowns such as ambiguous prompts and projection misalignment. Algorithm-level analysis and a user-centered study indicate improved text–image alignment and spatial precision, and support for iterative creative workflows in stage projection contexts.

items.title: Speedrunning Relational Foundation Model Pretraining
items.abstract: Progress on foundation model pretraining is gated by who can afford a trial, and relational pretraining is no exception. Recipes are developed inside individual labs, reported under private protocols, and do not accumulate. Speedrun leaderboards remove that barrier by decentralizing the search rather than the training run. The problem is fixed, the stack is open, entries are ranked by wall-clock time to a quality target, and one GPU is enough to hold the record. We introduce modded-nanoRT, the first such leaderboard for Relational Transformers. Which database to hold out decides whether the benchmark can resolve improvements at all, so we fix it by calibration, ranking six candidates by how sharply a 45-minute learning curve separates improvement from seed noise. We open the leaderboard with typed trilinear attention, a relational operator that conditions attention scores and values on the foreign key traversed, together with Muon and SIGReg. The recipe reaches the target in 305.63 seconds on one NVIDIA H200, 8.11x faster than the reference implementation, and wins 13 of 15 pairs outside the development database. We will release the benchmark, its frozen artifacts, and the record runs. Our code is available at https://github.com/kunumi/nanoRT.

items.title: Standards-Guided and Dependency-Aware Code-Level Documentation Generation
items.abstract: Automatically generating high-quality documentation for software repositories remains challenging: existing approaches largely treat documentation as unconstrained text generation, lacking explicit quality specifications, depending heavily on long-context prompts over raw code, and offering limited support for reproducible evaluation. We argue that code-level documentation generation should instead be a standards-guided software engineering task, in which documentation is generated and assessed against explicit, reusable quality requirements derived from authoritative standards. We define code documentation as natural-language descriptions of repository functions and classes, organized by source-code path. We present CODEDOC, a standards-guided and dependency-aware framework that identifies dependencies between code entities via static call-graph and AST analysis and constructs dependency-aware structured prompts combining local code context, repository paths, and documentation criteria drawn from authoritative standards and style guides. We further introduce an interactive LLM-as-a-judge protocol that supplies criterion-aligned feedback to refine generated documentation along fine-grained dimensions from formal and practice-oriented standards. Experiments on ten open-source Python repositories show that CODEDOC produces higher-quality documentation than RepoAgent and a long-context baseline under standards-aligned evaluation, with relative improvements of 11.6%-17.0% and 21.4%-29.6%, respectively, while consuming roughly an order of magnitude fewer tokens per documentation entity than the long-context baseline. A human study confirms substantial alignment between LLM-based and human judgments (Spearman's rho = 0.72), and the relative findings hold across different judge LLMs. Code is available at https://github.com/ControllableModel/CodeDoc.

items.title: STUDENTS OF THE FACULTY OF SPORTS SCIENCES E-SPORTS LITERACY STATUS AND E-SPORTS EXAMINING PARTICIPATION MOTIVATIONS
items.abstract: The primary objective of this research is to determine the relationship between e-sports literacy levels and participation motivations of students at the Faculty of Sport Sciences, who are the prospective professionals of the digitalizing sports industry, and to analyze how these variables differ according to demographic factors. A total of 296 volunteer students (126 females, 170 males) studying at Erciyes University during the 2024-2025 academic year participated in this study, which employed a relational survey model. Data were collected using the “E-sports Literacy Scale” and the “E-sports Participation Motivation Scale” and evaluated through t-test, ANOVA, and Pearson Correlation analyses. Findings indicate that the participants' e-sports literacy (=3.33) and motivation (=2.88) levels are above the medium threshold. On the basis of gender, technical literacy and intrinsic motivation scores of male students were found to be significantly higher (p<0.05); furthermore, it was determined that an increase in age and years of e-sports experience positively affects literacy levels. As a result of the analysis, a positive and moderately significant relationship was identified between e-sports literacy and participation motivation (r=0.490; p<0.01). In conclusion, it is observed that as students' cognitive competencies in the field of e-sports increase, their motivation to participate also strengthens. Accordingly, it is recommended that sport sciences curricula be updated to encompass the technical and academic dimensions of e-sports.

items.title: Study on Multimodal Data- and Explainable AI-Based Risk Prediction and Intervention for Postpartum Depression in Nursing Care Settings
items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate a nursing-centered dynamic prediction and risk-stratified intervention system for postpartum depression (PPD) using multimodal longitudinal data and explainable artificial intelligence (AI). Methods: A quasi-experimental controlled study included 300 postpartum women enrolled within 6 hours after delivery and allocated by admission sequence to AI-assisted stratified nursing (n=150) or routine nursing care (n=150). Physiological, behavioral, psychological, and social-support indicators were collected, with EPDS assessments on postpartum days 7, 14, 28, and 42. A hybrid model combined temporal convolution, long short-term memory, text and voice representations, and multilayer fusion; SHAP and attention mechanisms supported case-level explanations. Outcomes included time to risk identification, EPDS trajectory, remission among high-risk women, nursing workload, and internally validated model performance. Results: Risk was identified earlier in the intervention group than in the control group (1.21 +/- 0.68 vs. 4.73 +/- 1.92 days, P<0.05). Mean EPDS reduction by day 42 was greater (-5.62 +/- 3.14 vs. -2.13 +/- 2.87, P<0.05), and remission was more frequent (78.3% vs. 42.6%; chi-square=36.41, P<0.05). High-risk identification reached 92.0% versus 64.0%. Time per follow-up decreased by 34.7%, and nurses reported fewer women requiring daily follow-up and lower work-related stress. The model achieved an AUC of 0.864, accuracy of 0.82, recall of 0.77, and F1-score of 0.79. Conclusion: A multimodal explainable AI system integrated with risk-stratified nursing care was associated with earlier risk recognition, improved depressive symptom trajectories, and lower nursing workload. External validation and a fully randomized multicenter evaluation are required before broad implementation.

items.title: Summary of the Book
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter summarizes the main claims of the book. Section 2.1 lays out the proposed analyses of agency, consciousness, and sentience and explains how each analysis applies to AIs. Section 2.2 summarizes nine main open philosophical questions about AI welfare, as follows: How should one identify which desires contribute to welfare? Is consciousness required for welfare? Do simple AIs like Roombas have welfare? Do tiny neural networks satisfy the conditions of functionalist theories of consciousness? Does consciousness require rich representational formats? Could AIs experience bodily pleasures and displeasures? Are pleasure and displeasure essentially access conscious? Are simulated minds real? Are LLMs and related systems merely stochastic parrots? Section 2.3 lists the seven largest, most controversial claims made in the book.

items.title: Sustainable Plant Disease Management: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Sustainable plant disease management is essential for maintaining agricultural productivity, environmental health, and global food security. Climate change has increased crop vulnerability to emerging and re-emerging plant diseases, posing significant challenges for agricultural sustainability. Although synthetic chemical pesticides have long been effective for disease control, their extensive use is increasingly questioned because of environmental contamination, pathogen resistance, and potential risks to human and ecosystem health. Consequently, plant disease management (PDM) is shifting toward more sustainable and integrated approaches. Future strategies are expected to incorporate multiple disciplines, including: (i) biological control and microbiome engineering to enhance natural plant defense mechanisms; (ii) advanced molecular and genomic technologies, such as CRISPR/Cas systems, RNA interference (RNAi), and epigenome editing, to develop durable disease resistance; (iii) smart delivery systems for the precise application of antimicrobial compounds and defense elicitors; (iv) nanotechnology-based platforms for the targeted delivery of nutrients, pesticides, and biocontrol agents, improving efficacy while reducing chemical inputs; (v) digital and precision agriculture technologies, including remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostics, to facilitate real-time disease surveillance and targeted interventions; and (vi) agroecological practices such as crop diversification, soil health restoration, and climate-smart farming to enhance agroecosystem resilience. These innovations aim not only to suppress plant pathogens but also to build sustainable, adaptive, and resilient agricultural systems that address future environmental and biological challenges.

items.title: Sustained Human–AI Collaboration as a Developmental Continuum: Continuity, Adaptation, Positive Consequences and the Limits of a Twelve-Month Rule (DE/EN)
items.abstract: Conceptual research note / Konzeptionelle Forschungsnotiz This note examines how sustained intensive human–AI collaboration can be described without inferring effectiveness from duration, continuous model training from personalisation, or a new category of human beings from exceptional developmental trajectories. The proposed unit of analysis is a person's trajectory within a changeable AI working environment. Continuity, integration, adaptation on both sides and real consequences are considered separately. A normative admission condition for a personal working circle is then developed: at least twelve months of actually continued practice, understandable positive consequences and a qualification trajectory that has already functioned healthily. The health condition is non-compensatory: achievement does not offset harm caused or aggravated by the practice. It is expressly distinguished from medical fitness diagnosis. Counterexamples and testable research questions show why the admission rule establishes neither a natural boundary within the continuum nor general medical safety. Als Analyseeinheit wird der zeitliche Verlauf einer Person in einer wechselbaren KI-Arbeitsumgebung vorgeschlagen. Kontinuität, Integration, beidseitige Anpassung und reale Folgen werden getrennt betrachtet. Daraus wird eine normative Aufnahmebedingung für einen persönlichen Arbeitskreis abgeleitet: mindestens zwölf Monate tatsächlich fortgeführter Praxis, nachvollziehbare positive Folgen und ein Qualifikationsverlauf, der bereits gesund funktioniert hat. Die Gesundheitsschwelle ist nicht kompensierbar; Leistung gleicht durch die Praxis verursachte oder verschärfte Schäden nicht aus. Die Grenze wird ausdrücklich von einer medizinischen Eignungsdiagnostik unterschieden. Gegenbeispiele und überprüfbare Forschungsfragen zeigen, weshalb die Aufnahmebedingung weder eine natürliche Grenze im Kontinuum noch einen Beleg allgemeiner Unbedenklichkeit darstellt. He initiates the circle described in the separate declaration and therefore has an interest in the proposal. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with structure, literature comparison, argument development and translation; Gemini was used for separate critical text review. These tools are not authors or scholarly peer reviewers. The note is not an externally peer-reviewed article. items.title: Synthetic Selves for AI Agents? Lessons from Psychology for Agent-Based Modeling
items.abstract: The growing interest in using large language models (LLMs) as human surrogates and as components of generative agent-based models (GABMs) raises a fundamental question for computational social science: what does it mean to model a person? The present paper surveys current work that uses LLMs to simulate human participants, with particular attention to their ability to reproduce findings of social psychology experiments. We document both the recurring challenges and the attempts to mitigate them. We then examine the possibility of endowing LLMs with a synthetic self by focusing on two psychological approaches to selfhood: trait-based personality and narrative identity. Our survey suggests that current LLM agents perform relatively well when selfhood is operationalized by rigidly structured means such as personality questionnaires, but are less reliable when it is induced by an unfolding narrative. We relate this problem to the characterization of LLMs as Decontextualized, Engineered, Anonymized, and Disembodies (DEAD) and consider its implications for GABMs. Drawing on the distinction between makeist and non-makeist takes on simulation, we argue that while GABMs may serve as a powerful tool for exploring how certain assumptions give rise to emergent phenomena, they do not necessarily constitute psychologically valid models of human behavior.

items.title: Targeting Inflammatory, Fibrotic, Hemodynamic, and Metabolic Pathways in Chronic Kidney Disease: Emerging Pharmacotherapies and Precision Treatment Strategies
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive and heterogeneous disorder that remains a major cause of premature mortality, cardiovascular morbidity, and kidney failure worldwide. Although renin–angiotensin system inhibitors, sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists have improved outcomes, many patients continue to have residual albuminuria, declining estimated glomerular filtration rate, and elevated cardiovascular risk. This review summarizes recent advances in CKD pharmacotherapy, focusing on therapies targeting inflammatory, fibrotic, hemodynamic, endothelial, and metabolic pathways. Emerging approaches include glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, aldosterone synthase inhibitors, endothelin receptor antagonists, dual endothelin–angiotensin receptor antagonists, soluble guanylate cyclase modulators, anti-inflammatory therapies, anti-fibrotic agents, and metabolic modulators. Evidence from major outcome trials, including DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY, FIDELIO-DKD, FIGARO-DKD, SONAR, PROTECT, and FLOW, supports a shift toward layered, mechanism-based therapy. However, implementation requires careful patient selection, monitoring for adverse effects such as hyperkalemia, fluid retention, gastrointestinal intolerance, hypotension, and hepatic safety. Future CKD management will likely integrate early detection, biomarker-guided risk stratification, genomics, digital health, and artificial intelligence to enable personalized, multi-targeted treatment strategies and improve long-term renal and cardiovascular outcomes globally.

items.title: TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION PERSPECTIVES OF ITS EFFECT ON STUDENTS' ENGAGEMENT AND LEARNING OUTCOMES
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the perceived effects of technology integration on student engagement and learning outcomes in Physical Education (PE) among selected middle and high schools in Maryland, USA, during the school year 2023–2024. Employing a descriptive-qualitative research design, the study gathered data from Physical Education teachers and selected student representatives through a researcher-developed, validated open-ended questionnaire administered using Google Forms. Thematic analysis was utilized to identify recurring patterns concerning technology integration, student engagement, learning outcomes, implementation challenges, and educational leadership implications. Findings revealed that technology integration was perceived to enhance student participation, intrinsic motivation, collaborative learning, and the overall learning environment. Participants also associated technology-supported instruction with improved performance, constructive feedback, goal achievement, and better comprehension of instructional content. However, limited technological resources, budgetary constraints, curriculum alignment difficulties, insufficient teacher training, and technical issues emerged as significant implementation challenges. The findings further emphasized the importance of adaptive educational leadership, continuous professional development, collaborative decision-making, and responsible technology use. Based on these findings, an Enhanced Technology Integration Program was proposed to strengthen technological accessibility, instructional practices, teacher competencies, and institutional support. The study concluded that technology integration offered opportunities to improve Physical Education experiences, provided that instructional and organizational challenges were adequately addressed.

items.title: Technology, tasks, and production
items.abstract: This chapter develops the theoretical core of the book by treating artificial intelligence as a production technology rather than merely as a collection of digital products. It explains why the standard language of aggregate production functions is too coarse for understanding AI and why the task-based approach provides a more useful analytical framework. AI matters because it changes which tasks can be performed by labor, which tasks can be performed by capital, and which tasks require new forms of complementarity between humans, software, data, and organizational routines. The chapter introduces AI as a general-purpose technology and develops a compact formal model of task allocation, task shares, displacement, reinstatement, and the elasticity of substitution between labor and AI capital. It distinguishes automation from augmentation and clarifies the economic conditions under which AI produces wage suppression or broad-based prosperity. The central claim is that AI does not enter production as a neutral multiplicative productivity term. It reshapes the task content of production itself.

items.title: Testing Associative Creativity in Humans and Multimodal LLMs with Difficult-to-Name Visual Stimuli
items.abstract: We investigate associative creativity in descriptions of abstract visual stimuli by humans and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). While conceptual association is central to human communication, it remains unclear how humans and models adapt when visual stimuli become increasingly difficult to map onto familiar semantic concepts. We evaluate several state-of-the-art MLLMs and human participants along two dimensions of creativity, originality and effectiveness, using two datasets with controlled manipulations of difficulty. SilCC varies naming difficulty through progressively more complex combinations of abstract shapes, and PixCC varies difficulty through increasing levels of random visual noise. Results show that humans produce more diverse associative descriptions than MLLMs, including greater semantic distance, higher entropy, and more novel expressions relative to reference lexica. As difficulty increases, effectiveness declines in SilCC, and humans increasingly shift from holistic associations to descriptions of low-level visual properties in PixCC.

items.title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
items.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an étendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating post-LSST observing time and strategies for transiting exoplanets, Type Ia supernova cosmology, time-delay cosmography, and second-scale transients. The filter group explored broadband, medium-band, and narrowband filters for photometric redshifts, high-redshift large-scale structure, AGN reverberation mapping, Galactic archaeology, and emission-line imaging. The multi-messenger group explored follow-up of next-generation gravitational-wave and neutrino sources, including standard sirens, kilonovae, and Galactic supernovae. The technology group organized options by cost and lead time, including fast readout, new filters, a faster shutter, and summit edge computing. Cross-cutting topics included AI/ML, Chilean and Latin-American co-leadership, satellite megaconstellations, and weather and climate trends at Cerro Pachón. White papers and workshop talks are available through https://zenodo.org/communities/rubin2036workshop/ and https://rubin-observatory.github.io/Rubin-Beyond-LSST/pages/Rubin2036proceedings/.

items.title: The Algorithmic Agora: AI-Enabled Government Communication and Sustainable Development in the United Arab Emirates
items.abstract: Governments increasingly communicate with their publics through artificial intelligence (AI), yet media and communication scholarship has concentrated on newsrooms and platforms, leaving the algorithmically mediated communication of the state under-theorised. This study asks how a state institutionally constructs, coordinates, and accounts for AI-enabled strategic communication, defined here as the intentional, institutionally coordinated use of AI systems by government entities to inform, persuade, listen to, and build relationships with publics. It develops the AGORA framework—Architecture, Generation, Orchestration, Responsiveness, Accountability—which conceptualises the state’s AI-mediated communication system as an algorithmic public square and derives six propositions offered as theoretical expectations for subsequent testing rather than as relationships tested here. A six-phase reflexive thematic analysis, following a documented search and screening protocol, was applied to a corpus of 34 United Arab Emirates (UAE) and comparative documents (2017–2026). Every quantitative indicator was then classified on a five-tier provenance ledger distinguishing binding law, policy target, officially reported performance, independently produced benchmark, and untraceable claim. Four themes emerge: a layered governance architecture in which the communicative safeguards rest on strategy and non-binding ethical guidance because the federal data-protection statute excludes governmental entities from its scope; documented algorithmic communication mechanisms; officially reported sectoral performance and its provenance; and contextual benchmarking against Singapore and Republic of Korea. The findings show the UAE state operating as a front-stage communicative actor whose agenda construction, personalisation and responsiveness are computationally augmented and specify where institutional claims outrun independent verification. Because the design is documentary, public engagement, trust, and sustainable development outcomes are positioned as expected outcomes outside the framework and are not empirically demonstrated. This study contributes a transferable framework, a four-stage maturity trajectory, and a provenance protocol for research on AI-mediated government communication.

items.title: The Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Academic Achievement Mediated by Psychological Factors
items.abstract: This narrative literature review proposes an integrative dual-pathway model to explain how socioeconomic status (SES) shapes academic achievement through interacting psychological mechanisms. Drawing on allostatic load theory, central executive functioning, self-efficacy, and learned helplessness, the model identifies two interconnected routes: a cognitive depletion pathway, in which allostatic load overburdens the prefrontal cortex and constrains limited working memory resources; and a motivational pathway in which low self-efficacy and repeated failures develop into learned helplessness that undermines motivation for learning. Crucially, these pathways do not operate independently but dynamically reinforce each other. Cognitive depletion undermines motivational beliefs, while diminished motivation reduces cognitive engagement, forming a self-reinforcing downward cycle. This integrated framework offers a more ecologically valid understanding of educational inequality than single-factor explanations. Practical implications suggest that educators should implement integrated interventions that simultaneously reduce extraneous cognitive load (e.g., scaffolded instructional sequences) and foster self-efficacy (e.g., process-oriented feedback) to break this bidirectional cycle. As the proposed model remains theoretical, future empirical research using longitudinal and experimental designs is required to validate its causal pathways and inform evidence-based educational policies.

items.title: The Biology of Leadership:Self-Regulation, Relational Responsibility, and Sustainable Performance
items.abstract: Purpose: This article develops a conceptual account of how embodied self-regulation may contribute to responsible and sustainable leadership without reducing social relationships to biological mechanisms. Approach: A theory-driven, non-systematic synthesis connects selected research on stress, sleep, emotion regulation, recovery, and social interaction with relational leadership and organizational work-design perspectives. The source material is an educational lecture, not an empirical dataset. Conceptual contribution: The proposed framework distinguishes regulatory capacities, their behavioral enactment, followers’ relational appraisal, and longer-term collective outcomes. Physical recovery, emotional flexibility, attentional organization, and purpose are treated as interdependent organizing domains rather than a validated hierarchy or biological leadership profile. Regulatory translation names the contingent process through which individual capacities become socially consequential through listening, fair procedures, constructive challenge, and support for autonomy. Six untested propositions specify mechanisms, contextual boundaries, reciprocal influences, and evaluation criteria. Implications: Leadership development should combine individual practices with changes to workload, decision processes, and opportunities for recovery. Physiological indicators cannot establish ethical legitimacy, psychological safety, or leadership quality. Originality and limitations: The article offers an integrative process model and a research agenda, not evidence that the complete model is effective. Its contribution lies in making the capacity–enactment distinction explicit while incorporating non-depletion of people into the assessment of sustainable performance. Multilevel, longitudinal, and intervention research is required to examine the proposed relationships.

items.title: The Cyber Soul of Marcus Garvey: Conceptualizing Afro-Digital Ethics and Theory in the Garvey LLM
items.abstract: This essay is a small window into the unfolding creation process of a cyber Marcus Garvey built on Afro-digital ethics, Black epistemology, and the interdisciplinary framework of Black Studies. It borrows from critical fabulation, embodiment, deep learning, and oral history to form a theoretical and methodological structure for a Garvey large language model. Its key argument is three-fold: (1) It must find a way to inject Black knowledge and aesthetic into computer systems; it posits a theoretical and procedural approach to constructing an entity that empowers Blackness within the computational world Black Studies plays an essential role in this process; and (3) it cannot fail to take up this mantle of responsibility. This process may or may not be faulty, but its underlining goal is for Black Studies scholars to collectively build digital tools that educate, protect, and empower in a fast approaching and unrestrained AI world.

items.title: The DAI-P2P Protocol: A Five-Layer Conceptual Framework for Distributed and Decentralized Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Contemporary Artificial Intelligence is undergoing rapid structural centralization. Large corporations control frontier models, massive datasets, and the computational infrastructure required for training and deployment, creating unprecedented asymmetries of power and access. This paper introduces the DAI-P2P Protocol, a conceptual research proposal for a distributed and decentralized AI ecosystem designed to democratize access to computing and knowledge. The framework integrates five technological layers: a DePIN peer-to-peer network; asynchronous federated learning with Model Sharding; a Proof-of-Intelligence (PoI) consensus mechanism backed by stratified Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP); distributed storage on IPFS/ Arweave; and DAO-governed community evolution. The PoI consensus is formally specified as a two-stage hybrid validation: cryptographic verification via ZKP followed by a stake-weighted Byzantine-fault-tolerant quorum. A cryptoeconomic model based on the DAI-T token aligns individual incentives with collective network integrity through graduated slashing and reputation- weighted rewards. The protocol is formally compared against Bittensor, Gensyn, and the ASI Alliance, positioning DAI-P2P as a unified design that addresses current limitations in scalability, continuous-update mechanisms, and formal compute verification. A public open-source repository constitutes the first deliverable of the experimental roadmap. No operational deployment exists yet; all DAI-P2P capabilities reported in this paper are design goals.
